## Part 60 — Expected Defaulters, full week: Sunday is a day of its own, not folded into Monday

> "i said lets give all the expected defaulters to sunday for full week recoveries. am sure
> assignments fall there too bro" — the owner, 12 November 2026

Every defaulter's two cycle days (the weekday a loan was disbursed, and three days later) were
read through `rollSun`, one copy in `api/_lib/portal-core.js` (the live Expected Defaulters
list and its "Mgawanyo wa wiki / Weekly distribution" board) and a second, identical copy in
`api/_lib/expdf.js` (the Exp.Def Report, daily, weekly and monthly): `u === 7 ? 1 : u`, Sunday
rolled onto Monday, because nobody used to work Sunday. A loan disbursed Thursday, whose own Day
2 falls three days later on Sunday, was counted as if Day 2 were Monday instead; a loan
disbursed on a Sunday itself could never be anybody's Day 1; and the live clock that decides
"which day is today" rolled a real Sunday to Monday's slot too, so a customer actually due
Monday showed as due on the real Sunday as well -- one Monday obligation, double-counted as a
borrowed Sunday visit. "Assignments" is this same mechanism by another name: the dedicated
Defaulter Assignment screen (`assignments` in `portal-core.js`) carries no weekday of its own at
all (it is "today's deck, whoever owns it now", no day-of-week logic to speak of) -- the owner's
"assignments" is the Exp.Def list's own distribution board and day pills, which did.

**The fix.** Both `rollSun`s are gone; `primary`, `secondary` and the "which day is today" clock
read the real ISO weekday (1-7) everywhere they used to roll it. The live list's `dist` object
and its front-end twin in `VIEWS.defexp` (`public/app.html`, which recomputes the distribution
client-side so switching "Wangu / Wote" costs no round trip) both gained a `7:` key; the
"Mgawanyo wa wiki" board and the day-pill bar walk `[1,2,3,4,5,6,7]`, not `[1,...,6]`. The report
side's own Sunday-specific suppression -- `xdShowDay_`, which hid a leader's card's Sunday
column and tab unless real decks had been filed that Sunday, on the belief that the rotation
rolled Sunday away -- is gone too: Sunday now shows its column and tab exactly as Monday through
Saturday already did, filed or not. Nothing else moved: `assignFor`/`assignStrategy`
(`api/_lib/assign.js`, the role-rotation clock) read `days_elapsed`, never a weekday, and are
untouched; the week-walk itself (Part 57, `expdfPeriod`) already reached Sunday -- this is what
happens once it gets there.

**A customer whose true cycle never touched Sunday is not newly credited for it.** A loan
disbursed Friday has Day 1 Friday and Day 2 Monday, exactly as the calendar says -- never
Sunday, before or after this change. Money that happened to move on a Sunday for such a
customer is now correctly NOT counted as that customer's own cycle-day recovery, the same as
it would not be counted on an ordinary Wednesday either; before this fix it WAS counted, only
because the real Sunday's clock was forced to equal Monday's slot number. This is a real
behaviour change in two existing tests (`test/portal.test.mjs`): a customer's week recovery
figure, and a leader's card, both drop the ghost Sunday credit that only ever existed because
Sunday was pretending to be Monday.

**Checked.** A new test proves the positive case directly against `expectedDefaulters`: a loan
disbursed Thursday keeps Sunday as its own Day 2 (not folded into `dist[1]`), and a loan
disbursed ON a Sunday keeps Sunday as its own Day 1. The two existing weekly-report tests whose
numbers depended on the old fold were corrected to the true figures the calendar gives: the
first ("a finished past week counts Saturday and Sunday's own recovery...") was given a new,
locally-added customer (never touching the shared fixture every other caller of
`expdfWeekTables()` also uses) whose own cycle genuinely reaches Sunday, so the suite still
proves Sunday's own recovery is counted; the second ("the weekly card for an earlier week...")
needed no new customer -- it demonstrates the ghost credit's *removal* on the pre-existing C1,
whose own two days are Friday and Monday, and that Sunday's tab still appears, correctly empty,
the same as Saturday's already did for that leader. `test/pages.test.mjs`'s source-text checks
for the report screen were updated to match (`xdShowDay_` is gone; the day columns and day tabs
are never filtered). `npm test`: 1,513 pass.

**Reviewed** by two independent readers before this merged, converging on the same real gap:
`docs/HANDOFF.md`'s own first draft of this Part said "neither file imports `expdf.js`" of both
`/api/upload` and `/api/call` -- true for `upload.js` (its one `portalApi` call is hard-coded to
`'purgeSuperseded'`), **false for `call.js`**: `api/_lib/call-core.js` imports `expdfMine` from
`expdf.js` directly and calls it from two live, reachable handlers -- `api_callList`'s `'expdf'`
list (the GMO/MANAGER/BIKE rotation list a phone itself shows) and `api_callDailySummary`'s own
EXP.DEF% figure in the strip handsets poll every few minutes. This is the right design --
`call-core.js` sharing the one `expdfCore`/`buildRows_` definition rather than a third copy is
exactly "one definition of a rule, in one place" -- and it costs `/api/call` no new read or
latency (those two call sites predate this commit; only the arithmetic they run now differs).
But it does mean the fix reaches one of the two paths this repository is built never to get
wrong, and neither reviewer could find a test exercising it either way beforehand. Fixed: a new
test in `test/call.test.mjs` proves, through the phone's own two entry points, that a
Thursday-disbursed customer appears on the real Sunday and is correctly absent on the following
Monday. Both reviewers independently re-derived the day arithmetic for all seven weekdays (one
by writing throwaway scripts against the real committed modules, the other by hand against
`assignStrategy`'s bucket math) and the two corrected tests' exact figures, and found both
correct; one reviewer also live-reverted the `xdShowDay_` removal in a scratch copy to confirm
the `pages.test.mjs` checks actually fail without the fix, then reverted cleanly. `npm test`:
1,514 pass.

**What it costs.** No new read or query on `/api/upload` or `/api/call` -- `api/call.js` does
reach this fix, through `call-core.js`'s two pre-existing `expdfMine` call sites (now tested,
see above), but neither call site is new and neither runs a query it did not already run. A
front-end change: `BUILD 2026-11-12-d`.

**Not done.** Whether a customer worked a day early or late (off their own two cycle days, on
any weekday, Sunday included) should still count toward that week's recovery at all is a
separate question this change does not touch either way -- it never did, for any day of the
week, and nothing here starts.

## Part 61 — Clicking a name on Omba Likizo: the ask form's fields wired before they existed

> "clicking name on omba likizo - Imeshindikana / Could not load.
> Cannot set properties of null (setting 'onchange')" -- the owner, 12 November 2026

The very first time a name was ever picked on the Leave & Holiday ask screen, the screen failed
to load at all. `VIEWS.leavereq`'s own promise (`public/mod/leave.js`) set `HEAD` to the new
page -- with the request form in it, now that a name was chosen -- and in the same breath tried
to wire `#lvReason`'s change, `#lvStart`/`#lvEnd`'s input and `#lvSubmit`'s click. But that
promise resolves BEFORE `drawView_()` (`public/app.html`) ever paints `HEAD` into the real page:
`load_()` calls the view function and only THEN calls `drawView_()`, once the view's own promise
has settled. So the wiring ran against the PREVIOUS paint -- the one with no name chosen yet,
where none of those four elements exist -- `$('#lvReason')` returned `null`, and
`null.onchange = ...` threw. The throw rejected the view's promise, `drawView_()` never ran, and
the screen showed nothing but the generic failure message: exactly "Imeshindikana / Could not
load."

This is not a new kind of bug in this codebase -- it is the exact one HOPE Loan's own HEAD
buttons had on first write (the note beside `wireLnCs_` in `app.html`: "every other HOPE Loan
HEAD button ... had exactly this bug on first write"), and the one `portal-imprest.mjs` was
built to catch on the imprest request form's Submit button. Advance's own ask screen
(`VIEWS.advreq`) never had it, because it never wires anything itself: its one button,
`#advSubmit`, is wired from `wireForms()` in the core, and reads its own chosen staff from
`S.advReq.chosen` rather than taking it as an argument, so nothing needs wiring inside the view
function at all. Leave's ask screen copied advance's HTML shape but not that half of the
pattern -- and its own desk-wiring function, `wireLeaveDesk()`, already said on its own tin that
it was meant to be "one function for every button this module draws, on any of its three tabs":
the ask form's fields were simply never added to it.

**The fix.** `lvReason`/`lvStart`/`lvEnd`/`lvSubmit` are wired from `wireLeaveDesk()` now, not
from inside `VIEWS.leavereq`. `wireLeaveDesk()` is called from the core's `wireBar()` after
every paint (the same hook that already wired the desk's bulk-approve buttons and the report's
annual-days Save), so by the time it runs the elements are real. Every new lookup is guarded
with `if (el)`, the same as every other button already in that function, because it runs on
every tab's paint, not only `leavereq`'s. `leaveSubmit_` takes no argument any more -- it reads
its own chosen staff off `S.leaveReq.chosen`, exactly the way `advSubmit()` reads `S.advReq.chosen`,
so a post-paint hook can wire it with nothing to capture.

**Checked**, two ways. A new browser check, `tools/browser-checks/portal-leave-ask.mjs` (modelled
on `portal-imprest.mjs`), drives the real `public/app.html` in a real Chromium: it picks a name
for the first time -- the exact action the owner's report names -- and proves no script error
fires, all four fields are genuinely wired (not just present), the Other-reason field toggles,
the day count recalculates, and pressing Submit sends one `leaveRequest` with what was typed.
Run against the code as it stood before this fix, the same check times out waiting for the form
to ever appear -- the render throws before painting, exactly as the owner saw it. A second,
fast, source-level check in `test/pages.test.mjs` (part of `npm test`, unlike the browser one)
pins the shape of the fix: none of the four ids may be wired inside `VIEWS.leavereq` itself, and
`wireLeaveDesk` must wire all four, each behind its own `if` guard. Run against the original
code, it fails on the first assertion.

**What it costs.** Nothing on `/api/upload` or `/api/call`. A front-end change: `BUILD
2026-11-12-e`.

**Not done.** Nothing else on this screen was touched -- the desk and report tabs, already
wired the correct way since they were built, needed no change.

## Part 62 — A trigram index for legalFind's name/ref search

> "postgress is unsettled" -- the owner, 12 November 2026, with a Supabase dashboard showing a
> spike in Postgres errors and the exact query `legalFind`'s search box sends.

`legalFind` (api/_lib/portal-core.js) is the Legal tab's "search by ref, phone no and names"
box, behind the New-notice drawer. Its `ILIKE '%term%'` carries a leading wildcard, which no
ordinary B-tree index can use for the text match itself -- none of `defaulter_snapshots`' six
existing indexes (`schema.sql`, RUN-ME-011, RUN-ME-034) help with that part; they only narrow by
`team`/`snapshot_type`/`snapshot_date`. As the table grows with every day's upload, a name
search gets proportionally slower, however those other columns narrow it, because Postgres
still has to check each remaining row's text by hand.

Whether this exact query caused the dashboard's own error spike could not be confirmed from
here -- a chat has no database access and cannot open Supabase's own Postgres logs, which would
say what actually failed at that moment. What was confirmed, on a 2.27-million-row, 150-day
fixture built to match the live book's own shape (42 teams, 180 customers each, two
snapshot_types -- the same sizing logic as RUN-ME-034), with `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` before
and after a trigram index: a realistic search (a customer's actual name, or their ref -- enough
to find one person, which is what the screen is for) drops from 151 ms to 23–79 ms depending on
how specific the term is, and a ref search drops to under 3 ms. Said plainly, the one honest
cost: `legalFind`'s own floor is 3 characters, and a bare 3-letter fragment common across many
names can come back a little SLOWER with the index than without it (19.6 ms -> 41.8 ms,
measured) for a team-scoped search, because the old plan could walk a date-ordered index
backward and stop the moment it had enough matches, while the new one first gathers every row
sharing a trigram with the term. Neither number is close to a timeout either way, and a real
name or ref -- not three random letters -- is what this index is for.

**The fix**, `db/RUN-ME-054-legal-find-trigram-index.sql`: two GIN trigram indexes, on
`full_name` and on `ref`. No code change -- `legalFind`'s own query is untouched; Postgres's
planner simply has a faster path once the index exists. Built `CONCURRENTLY`, because
`defaulter_snapshots` is written by `/api/upload`: an ordinary `CREATE INDEX` takes a lock that
blocks every write on the table until the build finishes, which on the live book is almost
certainly minutes, not the thirteen and five seconds the two builds took on this file's own
test table with no traffic -- exactly the thing this repository is built never to do.
`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` is refused outright inside a transaction block, and the SQL editor
sends everything selected together as one, so the file says plainly, twice, to run each of the
two index-creating lines ALONE -- and if that is not followed, the failure is safe: Postgres
simply refuses with "cannot run inside a transaction block" and changes nothing, never a
half-built index or a blocked upload.

**What it costs.** No code changed, so nothing on `/api/upload` or `/api/call` beyond the one
honest cost above, which is on a portal-only path (`legalFind` is gated to the `legal` tab,
never reachable from upload or the call app). No `BUILD` bump -- a database-only change.

**Not done.** The migration is handed to the owner, not run by this chat (no database access).
Whether this was actually the cause of the dashboard's error spike is still open; if the owner
can open Postgres Logs around the time of that spike and paste the actual failing query, that
would settle it either way.

## Part 63 — A fourth arrow: loan apps joins sales, collection and recovery

> "Also Show the single rising and droping arrow in each of loan apps, sales, collection and
> recovery cards at dashbord against last weeks perfomancve" -- the owner, 13 November 2026.

The dashboard's own performance strip -- built earlier for "show average of sales%, col% and
recovery% performance... have the rising constant or dropping arrow symbol" -- already carried
this for three of the four: Sales %, Collection %, Recovery %, and their average, each with
`trendArrow` -- ▲ risen, ▼ dropped, ▬ flat, nothing when there was no prior week to compare.
Loan apps was the one left out.

It now carries a fourth tile, first in the row to match the order the owner named: **Loan
apps**, the week's count with the same arrow, and a sub-line naming last week's count for
comparison ("+5 maombi dhidi ya wiki iliyopita (24)"). It reads the SAME rule the "Loan
applications (Mon-Sun)" trend card directly below the strip already uses -- unassigned or
assigned stage, by the day the admin uploaded or the row was created (`appsInRange_`,
factored out of `appsTrend` in `dashboardFull`, `api/_lib/portal-core.js`, so the two can never
disagree about this week's own total) -- rather than inventing a second rule for what "an
application" counts as. Two other, different "apps" counts already exist on other screens
(the Call Agents board's bonus-driving count, deduped by track number and the CS roster; the
month report's intake count, which also counts stages past assigned) -- each answers a
different question for a different screen, and this change does not touch either.

**The one honest caveat, said plainly rather than hidden.** "Unassigned or assigned" is a
CURRENT snapshot, not a frozen one: an application that was unassigned last Monday and has
since been processed into approved or rejected no longer counts in last week's own total,
read today. The arrow can therefore move for a reason that has nothing to do with how many
applications actually arrived last week, only with how many of them are still unprocessed as
of right now. This is not a new property this change introduces -- the dashboard's own
"Loan applications" trend card beside it has always read the same way, and the point of
reusing its exact rule rather than a steadier one (every application created that week,
whatever its stage now) is that the strip's new number and the card's own total, on the same
screen, can never read two different things.

**What it costs.** No new read: `appsInRange_` only re-shapes `myLoans`, which `dashboardFull`
already holds in full back to last Monday for the sales-percentage arrow (`loanFloor`) -- the
apps comparison rides the same data already in memory. Nothing on `/api/upload` or `/api/call`
either way: this function serves neither. `BUILD 2026-11-13-a`.

**Not done.** No tip added to the `hints` table -- the new tile sits beside three others
already on the screen, labelled the same way, and needs no separate explanation. No real-
browser visual check (a chat has no database access to sign in and load a live dashboard) --
the number itself is proven by a direct unit test against `dashboardFullCompute_`, and every
inline script in `app.html`, this one included, is parsed by `test/pages.test.mjs` as part of
`npm test`, so the new markup is at least known to run without throwing. Whether the
"steadier" apps definition (every application created that week, regardless of its stage
today) would serve this arrow better than the card's own current-snapshot rule is a real,
separate question, not decided here either way.

## Part 64 — The open question from Part 63 answered: a false fall, fixed

> "not yet" -- the owner, 13 November 2026, on a screenshot of the arrow's first real screen:
> Loan apps 486, down from 741 the week before, a steep-looking drop circled alongside every
> other arrow on the strip and the trend cards beneath it.

Part 63 raised, and left open, exactly this: `appsInRange_` (unassigned/assigned stage, read
right now) is a CURRENT snapshot, so a week that is a week old has had time for a real share
of what it brought in to be assigned, approved or rejected -- and the moment it is, that
application stops counting toward that week's own total. 741 was never the true count of what
arrived last week; it was whatever was LEFT of it, read today, after six more days of being
worked. 486, read the same instant for a week barely begun, had almost no such time to drain.
The arrow compared a fresh number to a half-drained one and called the difference a fall.

**Fixed by giving the strip's arrow its own, steadier rule**, `appsArrivedInRange_`: every
loan whose upload date or creation date falls in the week counts, WHATEVER stage it sits at
now -- the same kind of fixed-at-the-time fact `SALES_STAGES` already treats a sale as once
it is approved, never retroactively undone by what happens to the loan afterward. The "Loan
applications" trend card right below the strip is untouched and keeps `appsInRange_` exactly
as it was: it answers a different, legitimate question -- how much of THIS week is still
sitting unworked, which is rightly a figure that shrinks as the week gets processed, and which
an admin genuinely needs for staffing. **The two numbers on this one screen are now allowed to
disagree, on purpose**, and both the server comment (`api/_lib/portal-core.js`) and the
client's own note above the strip (`public/app.html`) say so, so the gap is never mistaken for
a bug a third time.

Checked by rewriting the direct test from Part 63 with the exact case this surfaces: an
application that arrived last week and has since been rejected must still count toward last
week's own total (proving the fix), while the trend card's own weekly total still excludes an
application that arrived this week and has since been approved (proving the trend card's own
rule is genuinely untouched, not accidentally widened along with the arrow's).

**What was checked against live data, and what could not be.** The screenshot that raised this
was taken against `recovery-app.sync-book.net` -- the reserve server, which section 5 already
says may still read a different, copied database from the one every phone and upload writes
to. Checked again before touching anything: still DIFFERENT (`9372d032c6ca` against
`79e363955e75`), unchanged since the morning's 8-hourly report, so the 486/741 figures
themselves may not be live company data at all. The ARROW'S LOGIC is the same wherever it
runs, though, and the distortion it describes is real on its own mathematical terms,
independent of which database answered that screenshot -- which is why this is fixed now
rather than waited on until the two sites agree.

**What it costs.** No new read: `appsArrivedInRange_` reshapes the same `myLoans` the arrow
already held. Nothing on `/api/upload` or `/api/call`. `BUILD 2026-11-13-b`.

**Not done.** Whether the two different "apps" numbers now visible on one screen -- the
strip's arrival count and the trend card's backlog count -- need a word on-screen explaining
why they can differ (rather than only in code and this handbook) is not decided; the owner's
own next look at the real, reconciled book is what will show whether the explanation already
given is enough.

## Part 65 — The arrows asked for were on the cards themselves, not a separate strip

> "i meant arrows on cards of: Loan applications (Mon-Sun) ... Sales trend (Mon-Sat) ... Weekly
> expected trend (Mon-Fri) ... Weekly recovery trend (Mon-Sun)" -- the owner, 13 November 2026,
> naming the four cards by their exact on-screen titles.

Parts 63 and 64 built the arrow as a fourth tile on the small performance strip above these
cards. That was the wrong placement: the owner meant the arrow on the card itself, beside its
own title -- "Loan applications (Mon-Sun)", not a separate "Loan apps" tile elsewhere on the
page answering the same question in a different spot.

**Moved, not rebuilt.** Every delta the four cards now carry was already computed -- `dSales`,
`dCol`, `dRec` by Part 63's own performance strip, `dApps` by Part 64's fix to it -- so this is
a client-only change: `trendGrid` (`public/app.html`) takes an optional sixth argument, raw
HTML (unescaped, unlike its title and sub, which still run through `esc()`) rendered beside the
card's own title. Each of the four `trendGrid` calls now passes `trendArrow(...)` plus a short
delta note (`headDelta_`, a terser sibling of the strip's own `trendSub` -- the card's own
subtitle already says what the figures are, so the note stays to a single short line rather
than repeating a full sentence). The "Loan apps" tile is removed from the strip entirely, since
its own number now lives on the actual Loan Applications card; Sales %, Collection %,
Recovery % and the average stay on the strip exactly as they were before any of this started --
nothing asked for their removal, and the cards now carrying the same delta as a second,
consistent reading is an ordinary dashboard pattern, not a conflict.

**The Loan Applications card still carries two different apps numbers, on purpose, and now on
the one card.** Its own day-tiles and TOTAL read `appsInRange_` (unassigned/assigned stage,
right now -- "how much of this week is still unworked"); the arrow beside its title reads
`appsArrivedInRange_` (every application that arrived, whatever stage it sits at now -- the
steadier figure Part 64 built). Both sit on the same card now, which makes the divergence more
visible than when the arrow lived elsewhere, not less honest -- the arrow's own note (Rec/Sales/
Col cards: percentage points; Apps: a plain count, worded "maombi", never printed as a "%")
makes clear which question each number is answering.

**What it costs.** No new read, no server-side change at all -- every number was already
computed for the strip; this only changes where `app.html` draws it. `BUILD 2026-11-13-c`.

**Not done.** Whether the small performance strip should keep showing Sales %/Collection %/
Recovery %/the average now that the same three deltas also sit on their own cards, or whether
that is now redundant and the strip should shrink back to the average alone, is not decided --
nothing was asked to be removed from the strip beyond the Loan apps tile that was this change's
own, recent addition.

## Part 66 — Each day's own arrow, against the same weekday last week

> "i now need comparison of this Friday to that of last week" ... "arrows inside each day's
> card" -- the owner, 13 November 2026.

Part 65 put one arrow on each of the four cards, comparing the WEEK's total to last week's.
That was not what was asked: every one of the 28 weekday tiles across the four cards (Loan
applications, Sales trend, Weekly expected trend, Weekly recovery trend) now carries its own
arrow, each day compared against the SAME weekday the week before -- this Friday against last
Friday, not this week against last week.

**No new read.** Every figure needed for "last week's same weekday" was already sitting in
memory for the week-level arrow: `myLoans` (apps, sales) is read for the whole span back to
last Monday already; `myExpPrev`/`myDefPrev` (collection, recovery) are the same rows the
week-level arrow's own `weekPcts_` already holds; `stand` (recovery standing) already spans
both weeks in one call. Each trend's own day-loop just reads the matching day of `prevMon`
alongside the day it was already computing, using the exact same rule as that day's own figure:

- **Loan applications** -- `appsArrivedInRange_` (Part 64's steadier, stage-agnostic rule), for
  the same reason the week-level arrow needs it: a day a week old has had time to drain, a
  fresh day has not, and comparing the card's own backlog count (`appsInRange_`) across that
  gap would reproduce the exact false fall Part 64 fixed, just at the day level instead of the
  week level.
- **Sales** -- a point delta of the same %-of-daily-target the tile already shows, from
  `approved_date`, a fixed fact that never drains.
- **Collection** -- a point delta of Col%, from `colDay_` over `myExpWeek`/`myExpPrev` -- null,
  never a fabricated 0%, when either day has no sheet behind it at all.
- **Recovery** -- a point delta of Rec%, Monday-Friday only (`stand`/`recoveryByTeam`, the same
  rule the tile's own figure uses); the two weekend tiles, which already carry no percentage at
  all ("WE HAVE NO COL IN SAT AND SUN!"), carry no arrow either rather than inventing a third
  kind of delta for them.

**Client-side**, `tcell` (`public/app.html`) takes a new, optional fifth argument -- raw HTML,
unescaped like `trendGrid`'s own sixth -- rendered beside the day's own weekday label. The
other eleven callers of `tcell` are untouched; only the four day-tile loops pass it.

**Caught before it shipped:** the first draft defined `appsArrivedInRange_` (now needed inside
`appsTrend`'s own loop, not only afterward) in its old position, AFTER `appsTrend` -- a
`const` used before its own declaration line throws, and every test touching `dashboardFull`
failed with it (61 of them). Moved the definition ahead of its first use; `npm test` went from
61 failures to one real one (a source-pattern test in `test/pages.test.mjs` pinned to the
exact old four-argument `tcell(...)` call for the recovery card's weekday tiles, now five --
updated to match, since the SHAPE it exists to pin genuinely changed).

**What it costs.** No new read, no change to `/api/upload` or `/api/call`. `BUILD
2026-11-13-d`.

**Not done.** Whether the week-level arrow still earns its place on each card's own title now
that every day beneath it has one too is not decided -- nobody asked for it to be removed, so
it stays.

## Part 67 — A name beside the percentage, Early Collection on the strip, Inactive staff sorted last

> "Sales % [credit analyst] ... Collection % [todays collection officer] ... Recovery % [pmo
> rec officer] ... Performance · wastani [leading leader throughout the system with the best
> weekly average e.g Robert. Manager 80%] ... so add [name of the leading leader infornt of
> percentage like Amina 76%]" ... "add ealy col widget btn sales and col" ... "add ealy col
> cards between" Sales trend and Weekly expected trend -- the owner, 13 November 2026.

Two questions were costed and asked before anything was built, since guessing the shape of a
dashboard feature cost three redos earlier the same day (Parts 63-66): whether the
leading-leader ranking should be company-wide or scoped to the teams the viewer already sees,
and whether Early Collection should be week-over-week (matching its three neighbours) or
month-to-date (free, since the figure already exists). The owner chose the cheaper of each:
**scoped to the viewer**, and **month-to-date**.

**The leading leader, one name per strip tile.** Sales % names the best Credit Analyst this
week, Collection % the best PMO collection officer, Recovery % the best PMO Recovery officer --
each the one role the owner named. Performance · wastani reads EVERY role a team carries (the
same nine `ROLE_LABEL` roles the month report ranks on, now hoisted to module scope so the two
screens can never read two different lists of roles) -- "e.g Robert. Manager 80%" is a real
case: a Manager can lead that one tile on his own team's average with no sales, collection or
recovery role of his own. Scoped to the teams `teamAllowed` already lets this viewer see, never
the whole company -- that ranking is the month report's own leaders board, and that board's own
comment calls it "already the most expensive answer in the system"; this is the most-opened
screen, so it stays cheap.

**No new read, and no `weekPcts_` call per leader either.** The obvious shape -- call
`weekPcts_` once per candidate name -- would re-walk the whole scope's `myLoans`/`myExpWeek`
once per leader, which on an admin's company-wide view could mean dozens of full passes. Instead
one pass buckets the same three sources `weekPcts_` already reads (`myLoans`, the Mon-Fri
`colDay_` rows, `stand`/`recoveryByTeam`) by TEAM instead of summing them to one total; ranking
a leader then costs summing a handful of Map lookups over the teams they hold, not re-reading
the dataset. `weekPcts_` itself is untouched -- the strip's own `wkNow`/`wkPrev` read exactly
the code they did before Part 67, so nothing already shipped was put at risk to build this.
Wrapped in a `try`/`catch`: a mistake in the new arithmetic costs five fields, never the four
tiles that already worked.

**Collection's own precedence is read once, not twice.** The PMO-collection-officer-by-team map
(`colByTeam`, "the code wins over the sheet") used to be built right before the Orodha reads it;
it is now built earlier, before the performance strip, and both the Orodha and the new ranking
read the one copy -- not two independently-built maps of the same rule that could drift the way
CLAUDE.md section 2 warns about.

**Early Collection, month-to-date.** `perf.ecolPct`/`ecolExp`/`ecolCol` sum the same
`monthByTeam` the Orodha's own M. columns already read (ie/ic, the month ledger's early-col
cells), over the teams this viewer sees -- new arithmetic on data already fetched for every
dashboard load, not a new read. It is the one month-scoped figure on an otherwise
week-over-week strip, so the client labels it "· MTD" rather than mixing it in unmarked. A new
card sits between Sales trend and Weekly expected trend -- not a Mon-Sat grid like its
neighbours, since the month ledger keeps no day beside its own sum, and the card says so rather
than fake a daily map.

**Found by the estate-wide parity test, not guessed.** `test/snapshot-totals.test.mjs` runs
every dashboard-shaped screen twice -- once with the database doing the aggregate sums, once
with the same rows added up in memory -- and asserts the two answers are identical, since the
migration that installs the aggregate functions is run by hand and both paths are live at once
across real deployments. The new `perf.ecolPct`/`ecolExp`/`ecolCol` are exactly as
ledger-dependent as the Orodha's own `mEColPct` (one sanctioned, already-documented divergence:
without the migration the ledger never fills, so those fields read null on one side and a real
number on the other) -- but they sit under `perf`, a sibling of `teamPerf`, not a row inside it,
so the existing `withoutLedger()` helper's strip-list did not reach them and the comparison
caught four failures. Fixed by extending that helper, not by weakening what it checks: `perf`'s
own three new fields are now stripped from the comparison the same documented way, and a direct
assertion (`inMemory.perf.ecolPct === null`) proves what the stripping allows, the same way the
existing per-team loop already does for `mEColPct`.

**Inactive sorts last, everywhere the staff registry is listed.** "auto default deactivated
staff to be below on the staff list" -- `advStaff`'s one query (`api/_lib/portal-core.js`)
reads `staff_registry` ordered by `status` ascending, then `name`. 'Active' sorts before
'Inactive' in plain alphabetical order (A before I) -- the only two spellings
`advStaffSave`/`advStaffStatus` ever write -- so this needed no second column and no CASE
expression (PostgREST's own `.order()` cannot take one): the database does it in the one pass
it already made, at no extra cost.

**What it costs.** No new read anywhere, on any screen; the dashboard's existing reads are
unchanged, `weekPcts_` is unchanged, and the staff-list query already ran once. `BUILD
2026-11-13-e`. `npm test`: 1,519 pass.

**Not done.** Whether a leader who wins more than one tile (the same name under Sales % and
Performance · wastani, say) should be called out as such, or left to be noticed, is not
decided -- nobody asked either way. The card between the trend cards has no download/JPG
button its neighbours carry, since a single figure has nothing a screenshot would add over the
strip tile above it.

## Part 68 — The annual leave allowance resets each calendar year

> "26-day annual leave allowance should reset each calendar year." -- the owner, 13 November
> 2026, answering the question Parts 58 and 59 flagged rather than guessed: "a reset of the
> balance on a new year: nothing here resets it... whether it should is the owner's to decide."

`leaveBalance_` (`api/_lib/portal-core.js`) used to sum every Approved (and shown-but-not-
deducted Pending) request EVER, the one running ledger the Google Sheet's own `SUMIF` kept on
purpose, left that way until the owner said otherwise. Now it sums only the requests whose
`start_date` falls in the CURRENT calendar year -- by `nowMs`, the caller's own today, never
whatever stretch of history a report happens to be filtered to, because "remaining" has always
meant "what they have left to use, as of today", not "as of whichever dates this screen is
showing". A request from a past year is untouched in the table and in the report -- it stays
exactly as visible as it always was -- it simply stops costing the new year's allowance.

Both callers (`leaveRequestPage`'s own ask-form balance, `leaveReport`'s per-person balance)
already had `today` in hand; `leaveBalance_` takes it as a fifth argument (the year, as four
digits) and adds one `gte`/`lte` on `start_date` to its one query. The returned shape
(`{ annualDays, taken, pending, remaining }`) is unchanged on purpose, so a report or a screen
reading it needs no change of its own -- only what counts toward the sum moved.

Checked with a new test alongside the existing ones (`test/leave.test.mjs`): a staff with a
past year's Approved request reads a full, untouched balance this year; this year's own request
still counts exactly as it did before; and the past request is still there when the report is
asked for that past year specifically, proving nothing was deleted, only excluded from a
different year's own sum. Every existing leave test's own fixture dates sit inside one calendar
year already, so none of them needed changing -- the one new test is the one that actually
spans a year boundary.

**What it costs.** No new read: one more `gte`/`lte` on a query that already ran. No front-end
file touched, so `BUILD` stays `2026-11-13-e`. `npm test`: 1,520 pass.

**Not done.** Nothing else about leave changed -- the day count, the overlap guard, the
missing-table fallback, Expired-by-start-date, all stand exactly as Part 58 shipped them.

## Part 69 — A customer who pays in full stays on the Exp.Def Report, not just on the worklist

> "When a customer of expected defaulter pays full amount and no longer a defaulter, they
> dessapear from the expected defaulters report, yet they should stay there as of recovery so
> as to know recovery amount from difference of initial to current per each day by team or
> staff." -- the owner, 13 November 2026. Asked whether a paid-off customer's row still exists
> in the current deck (with a different status) or vanishes from the upload entirely, the
> answer was: "of today are of today by cycle and we got them from defaulters list so initial
> defaulter has initial of today accornding to their cycle appearance and latest report shows
> the last amounts leaving the reports of each day clearly showing what was recovered per
> expected defaulters b/se they cant run from when their initial file had them and their
> initial cycle placed them when and the initial and final amounts" -- the row stays, with a
> changed status; the harder case (gone from the upload altogether) was not in question.

There are two unrelated places this system tracks recovery, and only one of them had the bug.
The dashboard's own team-level figures (`recoveryByTeam`, `stand`) sum whatever rows exist per
team and day with no per-customer status filter, so a customer's absence from today's current
deck already reads as zero arrears -- full recovery -- by construction. The Exp.Def Report
family is different: `buildRows_` (`api/_lib/expdf.js`), the one definition of "a day's Exp.Def
row" shared by the portal's Exp.Def Report / leader cards (`expdfReport`, `expdfLeader`) and the
phone's own worklist (`expdfMine`), built ONE ROW PER CUSTOMER and, until now, only for a row
whose status contained CHRONIC/EXPIRED/DEFAULTER. A customer who paid in full carries none of
those on today's current deck, so the row -- and with it the day's own record of what they had
owed and what came back -- was dropped outright, from the report as much as the worklist, with
no way to answer "what did team X or officer Y recover today" for that customer ever again.

`buildRows_` now keeps a customer who is on TODAY'S OWN INITIAL deck (`baseBy`, the same
`{ref: arrears}` map the row's own `initial` figure already came from) regardless of what the
current deck now shows for them -- "they cant run from when their initial file had them." A
row kept this way carries a fourth status, `RECOVERED`, alongside CHRONIC/EXPIRED/DEFAULTER.
Everything else about the row -- `phase`/`role`/`cycle`/`leader`/`leaderPhone`/`opm`/`onToday`
-- stays exactly as `assignFor` computes it from the row's own `days_elapsed`, unconditionally,
the same as any other day: that is what the owner actually asked for ("by team or staff"), and
it is also load-bearing -- `periodRows_` and `expdfMine` both gate on
`RECYCLE_ROLES.includes(r.role)`, so a row with no role would have been silently filtered back
out by both, which a first draft of this change did by mistake before it was ever tested. Only
the `status` says the account is settled; nothing else about who owns it changes.

A worklist is not a report, though, and `expdfMine` -- read by the phone as much as the portal,
and the one function `/api/call`'s own `call-core.js` imports and calls (confirmed: its two
call sites, the `expdf` list type and the daily-summary strip's own Exp.Def figure, both go
straight into `expdfMine`, never into `buildRows_`/`expdfCore` directly) -- excludes a
`RECOVERED` row by its own, separate, one-line filter: nobody should be shown a call to make on
an account that is already settled, on the phone least of all. The report family reads
`core.rows` straight through `periodRows_`, with no such filter, so the two now legitimately
disagree on purpose: the Report counts a paid-off customer's recovery, the worklist stops
showing them a reason to call.

**Checked before settling on this, not assumed:** the portal has a SECOND, independently-
written function with the identical pre-fix filter -- `expectedDefaulters` (`portal-core.js`),
behind the "Expected Defaulters" tab, a name close enough to the owner's own words that it had
to be read, not skipped. Its own doc comments ("the officer working this list needs to know who
else is already on them"), its KPI label ("In the weekly cycle" = "chronic + expired +
defaulters needing follow-up"), and its status filter (offering only DEFAULTER/EXPIRED/CHRONIC,
no team or leader totals anywhere in the response) all say the same thing: this is the portal's
own mirror of the phone's worklist, not the "by team or staff" breakdown the owner described --
that breakdown is what `expdfReport`'s per-role sections and `expdfLeader`'s per-leader card
already are. It is untouched, on purpose, and its own net effect on who it lists is unchanged:
the broadened `buildRows_` filter plus `expdfMine`'s own narrowing back out reduces to exactly
the same CHRONIC/EXPIRED/DEFAULTER set `expectedDefaulters` has always used, so the two
worklists still agree with each other, one definition read twice rather than two that could
drift.

Checked with two tests, not one, given what calls `expdfMine`. In `test/portal.test.mjs`: a
customer who pays in full stays on the BIKE section's own totals and on their leader's own
`expdfLeader` card, credited for the full recovered amount, status `RECOVERED` -- and the SAME
customer is confirmed absent from `expdfMine`'s own worklist rows, with its totals unaffected
by a customer it no longer lists. In `test/call.test.mjs`, through the real call dispatch
rather than by trust in the call graph alone: `api_callList(..., ['dev','expdf'])` (a leader's
own list), the same call with `'team'` scope, and `api_callDailySummary`'s own `expdf` figure
all agree the row is gone from the phone, built against a fixture where the row would otherwise
have been sitting right on the list (today is genuinely this customer's own cycle day, and
their bucket is the exact role the test device is registered under).

**What it costs.** No new read: `buildRows_` already receives `curRows` and `baseBy`, both
already fetched by `expdfCore` for the `initial` figure every row has always carried -- this is
a filter and a status label on data already in memory, nothing added to `/api/upload` or
`/api/call`. No front-end file touched, so `BUILD` stays `2026-11-13-e`. `npm test`: 1,522 pass.

**Not done.** `expectedDefaulters` / the "Expected Defaulters" tab, as explained, matches
`expdfMine`'s own worklist philosophy and was deliberately left as it was. The harder case the
owner's own answer ruled out of scope -- a customer missing from the upload's current deck
ENTIRELY, not merely present under a different status -- still cannot be safely credited to a
specific leader: `assignFor` needs `days_elapsed`/`chronic_date`/`expire_date`, fields that live
only on a current-deck row, and a reference with none to read is a reference with no cycle to
place. Flagged for whenever it is asked about, not built on a guess.

## Part 70 — The worklists keep a cleared customer too, sunk to the bottom, not off the list

> "So even in call app if they clear they go down with status cleared.. same for the rest
> defaulters lists if possible." -- the owner, 13 Nov 2026, straight after confirming on a real
> customer (handbook Part 69's own open case, closed that same day: the loan system's own 12 Nov
> deck had already dropped them, nothing lost on this side) that a customer silently missing
> from a list is indistinguishable from one this system quietly lost.

Part 69 deliberately excluded a cleared customer from `expdfMine` -- "a worklist is not a
report... nobody should be shown a call to make on an account that is already settled." That
reasoning does not survive this follow-up: being shown a customer WITH a status saying they are
settled is not the same thing as being asked to call them, and the first is worth more to an
officer than silence. The exclusion is gone. `expdfMine`'s own filter is back to
`RECYCLE_ROLES.includes(r.role)` alone, so a cleared row flows through untouched -- and sinks to
the bottom of the list on the sort it already had (`arrears` descending; a cleared row's own
arrears is 0, the lowest value there is), with no new sort, no new field, nothing extra to get
wrong. The status label is renamed `RECOVERED` -> `CLEARED` everywhere it is set
(`buildRows_`), matching the owner's own word for it -- and, checked rather than assumed, both
`public/call.html`'s and `public/app.html`'s own shared status-chip classifiers already
recognise the literal string `CLEARED` as the green/"ok" bucket (`PAID|OVERPAID|CLEARED|...`),
alongside `public/app.html`'s own, separate, pre-existing use of exactly this word for a
customer who has "left the defaulter deck entirely" on the Promises screen. One word, read the
same way everywhere it already appears; this change did not invent it.

"Same for the rest defaulters lists" reaches `expectedDefaulters` (`portal-core.js`), the
portal's own "Expected Defaulters" tab -- the one worklist Part 69 checked and deliberately left
untouched, on the reasoning that it mirrored `expdfMine`'s own philosophy. That reasoning now
points the other way: it gets the IDENTICAL relaxation `buildRows_` already has (kept if still
Chronic/Expired/Defaulter, OR present on today's own initial deck regardless of current status,
status `CLEARED`), word for word the same condition. `assignFor`'s own role/leader computation
in this function was already unconditional (nothing to change there), and `recoveryOf` -- the
shared helper this function already called for `initial`/`recovered` -- already handles a
cleared customer's figures correctly; the only edits are the filter's own `||` clause and the
status label's own branch.

**One rule, read twice, is not the same promise as "the two can never disagree."** Caught by
review, not written down first and only found later: `expectedDefaulters` resolves "today's
deck" through `defaulterBook` -> `latestDeckAnyWeekday` -- the latest date of ANY weekday.
`buildRows_`'s own `curRows`/`baseBy` come from `expdfCore`, which is pinned to TODAY'S OWN
WEEKDAY and falls back to last week's same weekday when today's has not landed yet (a
deliberate, pre-existing, documented split -- `snapshots.js` itself contrasts
weekday-pinned-for-rotation against any-weekday-for-everything-else). On a morning when the
day's own deck is late, the two functions can resolve to DIFFERENT calendar days -- so the same
customer can read `CLEARED` on the portal's Expected Defaulters tab (which found them on a more
recent any-weekday deck) and be completely absent from `expdfMine`, the Exp.Def Report and the
phone's own list (still reading last week's same-weekday deck, which never had that customer at
all). The predicate text is one rule; the data under it is not, and this change does not close
that gap -- fixing the weekday-pinned-vs-any-weekday split itself is a separate, larger question
that reaches far more than this one status label, and is not attempted here on a guess.

**Checked before any of this, not assumed:** whether a front-end change was even needed, and
where. The phone's own `statusChip()` already renders `CLEARED` correctly (confirmed above), and
the `'expdf'` list view's own filter (`filterForView_`) narrows by role or by day for that view,
never by status -- so the call app needed NOTHING changed, and `CALL_BUILD` is untouched. The
Exp.Def Report's own per-customer status column (the leader's day-card, `xdDayBody_`) is plain
text, no chip, so it too needed nothing. Only the portal's "Expected Defaulters" screen
(`public/app.html`, `VIEWS.defexp`) rendered status with its OWN, screen-local chip function
(CHRONIC/EXPIRED special-cased, everything else a flat grey) rather than the shared classifier --
given a `CLEARED` branch there too, so it reads green like everywhere else; its status filter
dropdown gained the one missing option; and its "In the weekly cycle" KPI's own sub-label was
reworded, since it now also counts anyone cleared, not only who still needs a call.

Checked with two tests, rewritten rather than only renamed, since the claim they prove flipped
from exclusion to inclusion. `test/portal.test.mjs`: the same pays-in-full customer (`buildRows_`
Part 69 already covers) is now ALSO confirmed present on `expdfMine`'s own worklist, status
`CLEARED`, sunk below the real defaulter sharing their bucket, with the worklist's own totals
now crediting the same recovery the report does; a second, new test proves the identical thing
for `expectedDefaulters` directly, against the suite's own base fixture. `test/call.test.mjs`:
rewritten through the real call dispatch -- a cleared customer and a real defaulter in the SAME
bucket, so the sort order itself is under test, not only presence -- `api_callList('expdf')`
(leader-scoped and team-scoped) and `api_callDailySummary`'s own `expdf` figure all agree the
cleared customer is there, last, status `CLEARED`, and counted in the daily total. One real
fixture bug was caught and fixed before either test passed: two customers of the same team and
day given DIFFERENT `upload_batch` ids made one of them lose to the other under
`pickLatestBatch`'s own per-team rule (a real upload never does this -- one batch covers a whole
team's deck) -- fixed by giving both rows of the same type one shared batch id, the way a real
upload actually arrives.

**Reviewed by two independent readers before this merged, given exactly what it reaches** --
the sacred `/api/call` worklist, on a diff that reverses a decision shipped the same day. One
real, serious bug: `CLEARED` was being decided by eliminating substrings of the free-text
`status` column alone -- anything not literally containing Chronic/Expired/Defaulter fell
through to `CLEARED`, with no check of `arrears` at all. A blank status is not evidence of
payment, and this codebase already has the one rule for that exact question
(`api/_lib/settled.js`'s `isSettled`, built after a real customer sat on an officer's phone as a
defaulter owing one shilling while the expected book had her overpaid -- a stale or missing
status is unknown, never "paid"); this change reinvented a wrong one instead of reading the
right one. Proved, not merely argued: the suite's own long-standing `'555'` fixture (no status,
partially paid, 350 still owed) -- which the new call-app test already had to filter out "to
keep the fixture just the two customers it's about," without noticing why -- came back
`CLEARED`, rendered green by both front-end files' own chip classifiers, and SORTED FIRST on an
officer's own list (the sort is plain `arrears` descending; a mislabelled `CLEARED` row with
real, unpaid arrears is promoted, not sunk). Fixed: `isSettled(arrears)` is the one gate for
`CLEARED` in both `buildRows_` and `expectedDefaulters`; a row that is neither a recognised
defaulter status nor actually settled keeps its own status text, or `DEFAULTER` where it has
none -- the same fallback `statusWithPaid` already uses elsewhere, so it stays visible as still
needing a call rather than being told it is clear while it owes real money. Two new regression
tests reproduce the review's own scenario directly, through the real call dispatch and through
`expectedDefaulters`, rather than merely asserting the fixed line.

**What it costs.** No new read anywhere: every field a cleared row needs was already being
fetched for the rows that were never excluded. One front-end file touched for one screen's own
local styling and filter list, so `BUILD` moves to `2026-11-13-f`; `CALL_BUILD` is untouched,
confirmed by checking what the call app actually does with a status string before assuming it
needed a build at all. `npm test`: 1,525 pass.

**Not done.** The one case Part 69 named and this one does not reach either: a customer missing
from a day's current deck ENTIRELY, not merely present under a different status -- the real
example of this, found and closed the same day (above), was confirmed by the owner against the

## Part 71 — The all-time ghost: a customer missing from every deck still shows, status CLEARED

> "Checked loan system -- customer not there on thurrsday deck 12th nov 2026" ... "tell me
> latest date that customer was a defaulter of any status" ... "should reflect to alltime data
> past present and future" ... "so status column of such customers automatic becomes cleared if
> no longer in default list" -- the owner, 13 Nov 2026, on ref 4231948032: gone from BOTH the 12
> Nov initial AND current deck entirely, and still gone every day since.

Part 70's own "Not done" named exactly this case: `buildRows_`'s baseBy-presence check only ever
sees a customer who is on TODAY'S OWN initial deck -- a customer missing from BOTH decks
entirely leaves nothing in today's own data pointing at them at all. The only way to find one is
to ask the whole history: "who has this team ever had as a defaulter, whose newest row is not
today's" -- unbounded, "past present and future", not a recent-days window.

**db/RUN-ME-055** adds one function, `defaulter_ghost_rows(p_teams, p_known_refs)`, for exactly
that question. PostgREST's own query builder cannot express it cheaply: a plain `SELECT DISTINCT
ref` still visits every one of a team's rows to de-duplicate them (measured: 67-134ms on a
2.27-million-row fixture even with an index on `(team, ref)`, since Postgres has no built-in
skip-scan for DISTINCT). A recursive CTE that walks that same index one distinct value at a time
-- the loose-index-scan idiom -- answers the identical question as an Index Only Scan, no heap
fetches: 1.6ms on the same fixture. The function loops this once per team in `p_teams` (each its
own fast walk), then takes every surviving ref's own single latest `current` row.

**One round trip, however many teams -- caught before it shipped, not assumed.** A first draft
called the function once PER TEAM, cached per team; cheap for a single leader's own 1-2 teams,
but an unrestricted admin resolves to every team in the book (see below), and
`test/speed.test.mjs` -- which exists for precisely this -- caught it at 47 round trips against
a 7-trip budget for `expectedDefaulters`, and similarly for every `expdfReport`/`expdfLeader`
variant. The function already loops its own teams internally; the fix was to ask it for the
whole list in ONE call, cached by that exact team set, not to walk the set ourselves.

**Asked rarely, cached, and budgeted -- adjustments.js's own shape for the Iliyonasia register
on this same call path, not a new one.** `ghostRowsFor_` (`api/_lib/expdf.js`) mirrors
`readAdjustments`/`within_` precisely: a `WeakMap<db, Map<teamSetKey, {at, rows, pending,
missingAt}>>` cache (`GHOST_TTL_MS` 90s for a good read, `GHOST_MISSING_TTL_MS` 5 minutes for "no
migration run here" -- asked rarely, not re-logged as a Postgres error on every screen), in-flight
sharing (two callers in the same moment share one round trip), and a `budgetMs` honoured only by
the sacred path (`GHOST_BUDGET_MS` 800ms, passed by `expdfMine` alone; `expdfReport`/`expdfLeader`
and `expectedDefaulters` take none, since a report can wait out the rare slow read and the phone
cannot) -- and either way the read itself keeps running underneath and warms the cache for the
next caller, never cancelled. The one real cost (a whole team's upload genuinely missing -- not a
few customers, measured at 86-115ms with a disk spill) is paid once per cache window per team,
never per request; `db/RUN-ME-055`'s own function additionally carries a `statement_timeout` of
800ms as a second backstop. A database without the migration run gets the exact PGRST202 every
other such function here returns, remembered, and shows no ghost rows at all -- never a failed
request.

**Status is CLEARED unconditionally for a ghost row -- their absence from today's deck IS the
signal**, not a guess about whatever status text their last known row happened to carry (`isSettled`,
Part 70, is the gate for a row still ON today's deck; it does not apply here at all). The
NUMBERS stay honest: `arrears`/`initial` are the ghost's own last-known figure (15,500 for ref
4231948032, not a fabricated zero), `recovered` reads 0 -- nothing happened today to recover, and
a ghost is never credited with a guess. Role, leader and cycle come from `assignFor` reading that
same last-known row's own `days_elapsed`/`chronic_date`/`disb_date`, exactly as any other row --
the rotation's clock keeps turning on the calendar regardless of whether fresh data arrives, so
the officer currently holding that slot is still who is credited and shown, not whoever held it
the day the customer was last seen.

**Two more real mistakes, caught building this, not after:**
- The sort. `expdfMine`'s own "0 arrears sorts last" (#696) only holds for a customer CONFIRMED
  paid in full. A ghost's last-known arrears can be large -- ref 4231948032's own 15,500 -- and a
  plain arrears-descending sort would have put a customer nobody has tracked in months ABOVE one
  genuinely owing money today. Fixed: the sort is now CLEARED-last, arrears-descending within
  each group, not arrears alone.
- The admin. `ghostRowsFor_` first refused to run at all for `user.teams === null` (an
  unrestricted admin), on the reasoning that looping every team was a cost nobody asked for.
  That would have hidden the whole feature from the owner's own likeliest sign-in -- the person
  who asked for this the loudest. Fixed: `expdfCore` and `expectedDefaulters` both already fetch
  the full team list for other reasons; an unrestricted caller now resolves to that list instead
  of nothing, with the per-request-not-per-team round trip and `budgetMs` (not a team-count
  limit) carrying the actual safety.

**Checked.** `test/call.test.mjs` and `test/portal.test.mjs`: a customer with a real last-known
row ten days old and nothing since is found through the real call dispatch and through
`expectedDefaulters`, status CLEARED, their own last-known arrears shown, sunk below a real
defaulter sharing their bucket -- and, separately, confirmed ABSENT on a database without
`db/RUN-ME-055` run, exactly today's behaviour, no failed request. `test/speed.test.mjs`:
every existing budget still holds except one, raised in this same commit with the reason beside
it (below).

**What it costs.** One new index (`idx_def_snap_team_ref`, `CONCURRENTLY`, the same reasoning as
RUN-ME-054's own two) and one new database function, run by hand like every migration here --
every code path works without it, showing no ghosts. One new round trip where it is genuinely
needed: `expectedDefaulters`'s own speed budget moves 7 -> 8 trips (`test/speed.test.mjs`,
reason in the diff beside it); every `expdfReport`/`expdfLeader`/`expdfMine` variant already had
at least one trip of headroom and needed no change. No front-end file touched, so `BUILD` stays
`2026-11-13-f`; `CALL_BUILD` is untouched. `npm test`: 1,527 pass.

**Not done.** `test/speed.test.mjs` has no dedicated budget line for `api_callList(..., 'expdf')`
itself (only `'today'` and `'defaulters'`) -- a pre-existing gap in that file's own coverage, not
one this change introduced, but worth closing given this is the exact new code reaching that
exact path. Flagged, not built here, to keep this change to what it set out to do.

**Reviewed by an adversarial pipeline before this merged** -- a genuinely new query reaching
`/api/call` earns at least as much scrutiny as #696's own relabeling, arguably more. Eleven
candidate findings, each independently re-verified against the real files and a real local
Postgres rather than taken on the first reviewer's word; eight held up, three did not.

*Confirmed, and fixed:*
- **The one that mattered most: `p_known_refs` was sent as `[]`, always.** `readGhosts_` took
  the caller's real known-refs (today's own deck) and applied them only AFTERWARDS, in JS,
  never forwarding them into the RPC call itself. The SQL function's own exclusion
  (`candidates as (... <> all(p_known_refs))`) exists so its expensive half -- sorting a team's
  entire history to find each ref's latest row -- never runs on a ref about to be thrown away
  anyway; sending `[]` defeated that on every single call. Measured on the review's own fixture:
  1251 rows read, with a disk spill, instead of 100 -- a ~7x slowdown, paid on every real cache
  refresh (every `GHOST_TTL_MS`), not only the rare case the function's own comments describe.
  Fixed: `knownRefs` now reaches the RPC. The cache stays keyed by team set alone, not by
  `knownRefs` too -- re-keying on it would mean a fresh call almost every time, since today's
  deck is never the same list twice, defeating the cache for no correctness gain:
  `ghostRowsFor_`'s own JS-side filter already excludes a known ref from the final answer
  regardless of which request's `knownRefs` happened to fill the cache, so the SQL-side
  exclusion only ever needed to be a good accelerant, never the source of truth.
- **`balance` was never in the function's column list at all.** `expectedDefaulters` reads
  `d.balance` off every row it shows, ghost or not, and `balance` is a documented field
  (`docs/REPORT-PAYLOADS.md`) -- so a ghost's balance silently read as a fabricated 0 in
  production, contradicting this codebase's own rule for exactly this ("a figure that is not
  known is never invented"). The test suite's own looser mock (below) is why nothing caught it.
  Fixed: `balance numeric` added to the function's `RETURNS TABLE` and its `SELECT`.
- **The week was blind to the whole feature.** `expdfWeekCompute_`'s own per-day loop never
  called `ghostRowsFor_` at all, so a ghost that showed correctly on day and month vanished with
  no note the moment the Exp.Def Report or a leader's card was switched to week -- exactly the
  owner's own "same for the rest defaulters lists if possible," not actually kept for this one.
  Fixed, but deliberately narrow: a ghost reaches the week only through the week's own TODAY
  iteration, and only when the week being viewed is the live one. `db/RUN-ME-055`'s function
  answers "missing from the team's latest data right now" -- it has no concept of a past day at
  all, so asking it for a CLOSED week would mean judging history by a fact that is only true
  today, which is the one thing this feature's own design refuses to do anywhere else.
- **Two test-mock gaps that let the above pass silently.** `test/snapshot-totals-rpc.mjs`'s own
  ghost mock spread the whole fixture row (`{...row}`) instead of projecting to the real
  function's columns -- the one mock in that file not built "clause for clause... as Postgres
  will answer," which is why the missing `balance` column never showed up as a failure. And the
  GHOST1/ref-'222' tests' own fixture gave `ASSIGN_ACTIVE` and `ASSIGN_CHRONIC` the same first
  bucket, so a regression that fed `assignFor` the CLEARED display status instead of the row's
  real one would have landed on the identical role either way, unnoticed. Both fixed, with new
  assertions (`row.balance`, `row.cycle`/`ghost.fuStatus`) that fail if either regresses.
- **Two minor, real findings, fixed alongside:** `ghostTeams` was never deduplicated before
  being sent to the RPC -- a hand-typed, non-unique `access_codes.teams` array repeating one
  team made that team's ghosts count twice, double-counting `sumExpdf`'s plain-reduce totals
  (never its Set-deduped customer count). And nothing in the suite exercised
  `withinMs_`/`GHOST_BUDGET_MS`'s own timeout-abandonment -- the one property this whole
  budgeted-read design depends on for the sacred path's safety -- so a future refactor that
  quietly broke the race (confirmed: replacing it with a plain `.catch()` passes every existing
  test) would have gone unnoticed. Both fixed: the former with a one-line `[...new Set(...)]` in
  every place `ghostTeams` is built; the latter with a new test modelled on the identical check
  `test/zone.test.mjs` already has for `zoneOfSignIn`.
- **A nit taken too, being free:** the function gave up `STABLE` for an in-body `set local
  statement_timeout`, which Postgres genuinely refuses inside a `STABLE` function -- but a
  function-level `SET` clause works under `STABLE` with byte-identical output (verified side by
  side), and this function only ever reads. Changed for accuracy, not behaviour. One real thing
  the checking of this nit turned up: neither form of `SET` actually re-arms Postgres's own
  statement-timeout clock for the single top-level call that invokes the function -- a
  statement's timeout latches once, before the function body runs. This does not weaken the
  actual defence here, which has always been the JS-side race (`withinMs_`); it is noted in the
  function's own comment so nobody mistakes the database-side `SET` for the one guarantee.

*Checked and refuted, not acted on* (an adversarial pipeline cuts both ways): the function's
exact-match `d.team = v_team` looked like the exact team-name-drift bug class that has already
caused two blackouts here (CLAUDE.md section 2) -- refuted, because `p_teams` is never a raw,
user-typed list; both call sites resolve it from `user.teams` or the `teams` table's own
canonical rows first. The cache key's `\u0001` join looked unescaped against a team name that
itself contained that separator -- technically true, but not practically exploitable (the same
idiom is already used elsewhere in this codebase for similar data, and no team name reachably
contains a control character). A second, separate team-case-normalization claim at the same
line as the dedup fix -- refuted, on tracing a normalization layer upstream of both real call
sites that the finding had not followed back to.

`npm test`: 1,529 pass (two new tests; existing ones adjusted where the fix itself changed what
they were asserting). `test/speed.test.mjs`: the live week's own ghost lookup measured as one
more round trip where it now genuinely runs (12 -> 13 trips on the dedicated five-day week
check, comment updated in the diff beside it); every other existing budget held unchanged. No
front-end file touched; `BUILD`/`CALL_BUILD` still untouched.

## Part 72 — Early Collection joins the week: a rising-and-falling tile, a five-day card

> "At dashboard Early Collection % · MTD should be of week and showing rise or fall as the other
> widgets" ... "And the card Early Collection, mwezi hadi sasa, si kwa siku / month to date, not
> by day should be of 5 days as the others" ... "Like loan apps, sales, col and rec" — the owner,
> 14 Nov 2026.

#691 (Part 67) had put Early Collection on the strip as month-to-date on purpose — the owner was
shown the cost of each shape beforehand and chose the cheaper one. This reverses that choice, in
the owner's own words, which is theirs to do: the strip tile now reads the WEEK, with the same
▲/▼/▬ arrow every other tile carries, and the standalone card below it is no longer a single
static month figure but a five-day Monday–Friday grid, built to the exact pattern "loan apps,
sales, col and rec" already share — a `trendGrid` of day tiles, each with its own arrow against
the SAME WEEKDAY exactly one week earlier (#690's own rule, never a week-total spread across
days).

**Built by mirroring what this screen already pays for, not by inventing a second way to ask
for a week.** `expectedTotalsInRange(db, { type: 'initial', ... })` is the one function every
week-sized read on this screen already goes through (it is what `expWeek`/`expPrev`/`colTrend`
already call); a new `ecolTrend` array reads it exactly the way `colTrend` does, through a new
`ecolDay_` helper that tags the Iliyonasia-register correction `'expected-initial'` — the SAME
tag `earlyExp`/`tomorrowSnap` already use a few lines below it, and deliberately not
`colDay_`'s own `'expected-current'`, since mixing the two books' corrections is exactly what
this file already warns against doing. **This week is read unbounded; last week is read under
`dashPrevBudget_`** — the identical asymmetry `expWeek`/`expPrev` already carry, for the reason
written beside them: a real production morning once saturated this database badly enough that
"last week" reads (needed only for an arrow) had to be time-boxed to a race that falls back to
`[]`, while "this week" (the tile's own headline number) cannot be skipped. No new safety
mechanism was built; the existing one was extended to one more pair of reads. `perf.ecolPct` and
its new sibling `perf.dEcol` are now computed from `ecolTrend`'s own sums, the same way the
other three strip deltas (`dSales`/`dCol`/`dRec`) are computed from their own trend arrays, not
from `weekPcts_` — that shared function's own `wkPrev.hasData` gate is specifically about the
other three metrics' own all-or-nothing week comparison, and reusing it for Early Collection
would have been the wrong rule borrowed for the wrong reason. `perf.ecolExp`/`perf.ecolCol` (the
old month ledger's own two raw totals, read by nothing else in the codebase — checked) are
removed outright, not kept and ignored.

**What this unties.** The old tile read `monthByTeam`, the per-team-per-day cache kept in
`settings` under `MONTH_LEDGER_<yyyy-mm>` — agg-only, `null` on a database without the SQL
aggregate migration run, which is why the tile could read "not yet" for a whole month at a time
on a database that had never filled it. `expectedTotalsInRange`'s `type: 'initial'` read carries
its OWN raw-row fallback (`expFoldRead`/`snapshotsInRange`) and
never returns null for lack of a migration, the same as `expWeek`/`expPrev` never do. The new
figures are no more migration-sensitive than the three they now sit beside, so
`test/snapshot-totals.test.mjs`'s own estate-wide parity check (migrated vs. unmigrated, byte for
byte) now verifies `ecolPct`/`dEcol` for free — `PERF_LEDGER_KEYS`, the list that used to carve
those two fields out of that check, is removed entirely, not merely edited; the Orodha's own
ledger-level `mEColPct`/`mColPct`/`mRecPct` (`LEDGER_KEYS`, a different list, a different screen)
are untouched.

**What it costs.** Two more reads where the screen already pays for this shape of read: **+2
round trips, 0 new rows**, on the MIGRATED-world budget only (`test/speed.test.mjs`) —
`dashboardFull` 37→39 trips for an unrestricted admin, 36→38 for a one-team officer, carried
unchanged onto the "Company line, cold" row that shares the dashboard's own numbers by its own
design comment. The UNMIGRATED-world columns had headroom already and needed no change. Reasons
are written beside the three changed rows, as this file's own rule requires. No read was added
to `/api/upload` or `/api/call` — this function serves neither.

**Checked.** `test/portal.test.mjs`: the existing per-day-arrow test gained two fixture rows
(today-Friday and last-Friday, type `'initial'`) and new assertions on `d.ecolTrend` (the day's
own pct and arrow, and a not-yet-uploaded day reading null) and on `d.perf.ecolPct`/`d.perf.dEcol`;
the existing team-scoping test for the strip tile was rewritten end to end (the old cold/warm
ledger-filling dance no longer applies) to prove the week figure is read among the teams the
viewer sees, and null when unmeasured, using the suite's own already-tabbed `GMO` fixture.
`npm test`: 1,529 pass, the same count as Part 71 left it — both changed tests were extensions
and rewrites of existing ones, not new blocks. **Not done:** no real-browser check — this chat
has no database to sign into and load a live dashboard with; `public/app.html`'s inline script is
still parsed source-side by `test/pages.test.mjs`, part of `npm test`, which is what is actually
