## Part 73 — The Loan pipeline widget leaves; Expected Defaulters recovery, Monday to Sunday, arrives

> "Remove the Loan pipeline widget at dashboard replace with expected defaulters recovery
> cards Monday to Sunday with rising and falling arrows as usual" ... asked whether this meant
> the per-officer figure the Exp.Def Report itself shows, or a team-wide tile: "Am talking of
> the days performance Monday to Sunday like the cards showing summary of sales and collection
> per day" -- the owner, 14 Nov 2026.

The all-time, eight-stage pipeline funnel is gone from the dashboard, replaced by a sixth
weekday trend card -- team-wide, day by day, the identical `trendGrid` shape as the five
beside it -- plus a strip-free title arrow, never the per-officer breakdown the dedicated
Exp.Def Report shows (`buildRows_`/`expdfWeekCore`, `api/_lib/expdf.js`). Costed and asked
before anything was built: the dashboard holds no per-customer rows at all, so a true
per-officer figure would have meant either reading the whole week's raw decks the way
`expdfWeekCore` does for the Exp.Def Report (about 13 more round trips, nearly doubling this
screen's own budget) or re-deriving the rotation that decides WHO owns a customer
(`assign.js`'s configurable `assignFor`) a second time, in SQL -- exactly the "two
implementations that can disagree" CLAUDE.md section 2 already names two real blackouts for.
The owner's answer, once asked, ruled both out: team-wide, no officer breakdown.

**`db/RUN-ME-056`** adds one function, `expdf_recovery_totals(p_dates, p_weekdays, p_teams)`,
answering the one question this needed: of the customers that count as Expected Defaulters --
Chronic, Expired or (Partial) Defaulter by status text, OR present on that SAME day's own
initial deck at all (`buildRows_`'s exact membership test, ported, never the rotation on top
of it) -- what was recovered, per team, per day. **The one real arithmetic difference from
"Weekly recovery trend" beside it, kept on purpose:** `recovered` here is a SUM OF
PER-CUSTOMER, CLAMPED differences (`buildRows_`'s own `Math.max(0, initial - arrears)`), never
the team-total subtraction `recoveryByTeam`/`recovery_standing` use -- a customer whose arrears
GREW contributes nothing (never a negative), while the team-total figure nets that loss
against a stranger's gain on the exact same rows. **The two cards are allowed to disagree on
the same day, on purpose**, the same way #688 let the dashboard's own loan-apps arrival count
and backlog count disagree rather than force a wrong agreement -- proved directly in
`test/portal.test.mjs`: two customers on one team, one recovering 60,000 and one losing
50,000 to 80,000, read 60,000 recovered here and 30,000 on "Weekly recovery trend", off the
identical two decks.

**Measured on a 2,268,000-row fixture** sized like RUN-ME-054/055's own (42 teams, 150 days,
two snapshot_types, ~180 customers a team a day), built and queried directly against a real
local PostgreSQL before this shipped, not assumed: a full week, every team, the worst case an
unrestricted admin's own dashboard asks for, reads 294 rows in ~210ms; the common case -- one
team's own week -- in ~43ms. One round trip either way, however many teams. `set
enable_bitmapscan = off set enable_seqscan = off` is copied from `recovery_standing`'s own
proven defensive planner hint, reading the same table the same way; `set statement_timeout =
'2000ms'` is a backstop at about four times the measured worst case. **A real mistake caught
building this, before any of it was trusted:** the first synthetic fixture gave every team's
customers the SAME short reference strings ('CUST-7-1' on both TEAM1 and TEAM2); `ref` is this
system's own global customer key everywhere else it is used (`idx_def_snap_ref`, the ghost-row
feature's own ref-keyed rescue, #697), so a team-colliding fixture is not a realistic one --
with it, the function's own `distinct on (ref)` collapsed forty-two teams' worth of rows into
one, which a team-prefixed fixture (the realistic shape) immediately cleared. Nothing in the
shipped function changed; the fixture was wrong, not the SQL -- but it is why this entry says
"measured," not "written and assumed."

`api/_lib/snapshot-totals.js`'s `expdfRecoveryTotals` calls the new function the way every
other optional aggregate here does: a missing function (RUN-ME-056 not yet run) is remembered
for five minutes and answered `null`, never a failed request -- and `null`, not `[]`, on
purpose, so a budget timeout and a database without the migration read identically downstream
(no arrow, no guess), the same distinction `within_`'s other callers on this screen already
rely on. **This week is read unbounded** (the card's own headline figures); **last week is
read under `dashPrevBudget_`**, the identical asymmetry `expWeek`/`expPrev`/`ecolWeek`/
`ecolPrev` already carry, for the reason written beside them (a real production morning once
saturated this database; a "last week" read exists only to feed an arrow and must never hold
up the page).

**What it costs.** `stageCounts`'s own dashboard read (the pipeline funnel's eight-counts-or-
one-grouped-call) leaves with the widget it existed for; two new reads take its place. Net
`test/speed.test.mjs` change: **+1 round trip** on the migrated-world dashboard budget (37 ->
39 for Early Collection earlier the same day, -> 40 here: +2 for the new reads, -1 for the one
removed), 0 new rows. The unmigrated-world columns already had headroom and needed no change
-- in that world `expdf_recovery_totals` is equally unavailable, so the two new reads cost the
same one failed call each there too, while the eight-call `stageCounts` loop they replace is
gone; the net there is cheaper, not costed into the ceiling since nothing failed by leaving it
be. No read on `/api/upload` or `/api/call` -- this function serves neither. `stageCounts` the
FUNCTION stays; only the dashboard's own call to it is gone -- the diagnosis screen's probe
still uses it.

**Checked.** A new mock, `EXPDF_RECOVERY_RPC` (`test/snapshot-totals-rpc.mjs`), mirrors
`db/RUN-ME-056` clause for clause (the same idiom `recoveryStandingMirror_`/
`DEFAULTER_GHOST_ROWS_RPC` already use, projected to the real function's exact column list,
not the whole fixture row -- #697's own review caught a real bug that shape of mistake causes).
Added to the "team-day totals" migrated world in `test/speed.test.mjs`. A dedicated test in
`test/portal.test.mjs` proves the per-customer clamp against `recTrend`'s own team-total figure
on shared rows, team scoping, the day-by-day and week-total arrows, an unmeasured day, and the
no-migration fallback. `npm test`: 1,530 pass (one new test). `BUILD 2026-11-14-b`;
`CALL_BUILD` untouched -- nothing on the call app's own screens changed. **Not done:** no
`hints` table tip (the card sits among five others already carrying the same shape, needing no
separate introduction); no real-browser check -- no database to sign into from here;
`public/app.html`'s inline script is still parsed source-side by `test/pages.test.mjs`, part of
`npm test`. Whether the card should be clickable to open its own customer list, the way "Weekly
recovery trend" is, was not asked for and is not built.

## Part 74 — Expected Defaulters recovery, corrected before it was ever run: driven by the initial deck

> "not yet, i want the weekly cyle to be facts of the no of defaulters we really had, not who
> remained so the lists per day must come from initial files i think" -- the owner, 14 Nov
> 2026, having read Part 73's own `db/RUN-ME-056` text but not yet run it.

Part 73's own first cut drove the day's population from the CURRENT deck: a row counted when
its current status read Chronic, Expired or (Partial) Defaulter, OR it matched that day's
initial deck. That is "who remained" -- a customer on day D's own INITIAL deck who had vanished
from day D's CURRENT deck ENTIRELY was never reached at all, because the function never
iterated the initial deck on its own, only used it as a side check against rows the current
deck happened to still have. The owner's own correction inverts the whole shape: **the initial
deck is now the sole driving table.** Every ref on a day's own initial deck IS a defaulter that
day, full stop, no status check at all (the initial deck carries no status column to check);
the current deck is only ever looked UP for that ref, never iterated by itself. A ref with no
matching current row that day reads as fully recovered -- current 0, recovered the whole
initial amount -- the way #697's own order already reads an absence everywhere else on this
system ("status column of such customers automatic becomes cleared if no longer in default
list"), applied here per day instead of only to "today." The old current-only branch (a
defaulter-ish status with no matching initial row that day) is gone outright: under "the lists
per day must come from initial files," a ref that day's own initial file never named is not
that day's to count, whatever its current status says.

**`db/RUN-ME-056` is revised in place, not renumbered** -- the owner had read it but had not
yet run it anywhere, so there is nothing live to migrate away from; the file's own "safe to
re-run" already covers this. Re-measured on the identical 2,268,000-row fixture Part 73 used:
294 rows, ~210ms the worst case (every team, a full week), ~50ms the common one-team case --
unchanged within noise, since driving from initial instead of current changes WHICH rows are
kept, not how many decks are read or how they are batch-resolved.

**Checked** with two new customers added directly to the dedicated test from Part 73, proving
the two cases that flipped: a customer on the initial deck with no matching current row at all
(now fully recovered, where the old version excluded them completely) and a customer on the
current deck with a Chronic status and no matching initial row (now excluded outright, where
the old version counted them as a wash). The existing matched-row cases (a real recovery, an
arrears increase clamped to zero) are unchanged, since both rows were always on both decks.
`EXPDF_RECOVERY_RPC` (`test/snapshot-totals-rpc.mjs`) is rewritten to drive from `ini` the same
way, never visiting a current-only row at all. `npm test`: 1,530 pass (same test rewritten with
a longer, more precise name, not a new one added). `BUILD 2026-11-14-c` (the card's own
subtitle text changed to describe the new rule); `CALL_BUILD` untouched.

**Flagged, not changed:** the dedicated Exp.Def Report's own week (`buildRows_`/
`expdfWeekCore`, `api/_lib/expdf.js`) has the IDENTICAL structural gap this correction just
closed on the dashboard -- its own code comment already says so plainly ("A customer with no
current row at all ... is the one case this cannot reach"). That function feeds the phone's own
sacred call path (`expdfMine`, read by `/api/call`) as well as the portal's report, so changing
its own driving table is a materially bigger, riskier change than this one (a brand-new,
not-yet-run dashboard function) was -- not undertaken here, not without being asked. Whether
"the lists per day must come from initial files" should extend there too is the owner's to say.

## Part 75 — Expected Defaulters: a customer never once on a current row still shows, status CLEARED

> "a customer who drops off the current deck entirely shouldnt be invisible anywhere" -- the
> owner, 14 Nov 2026, following directly from Part 74's own correction.

#697's own ghost mechanism (`ghostRowsFor_`, `db/RUN-ME-055`) rescues a customer missing from
TODAY's current deck who has SOME current-type row anywhere in this team's history -- its own
all-time walk needs that to exist, since the join behind it (`... and d.snapshot_type =
'current'`) only ever matches a current-type row. A customer whose VERY FIRST appearance
anywhere is today's own initial deck -- never once on a current-type row, in the whole history
-- is the one case even that mechanism cannot reach: the walk finds the ref as a candidate, the
join behind it returns nothing for it, and `buildRows_`'s own filter (over `curRows`, which this
ref was never in to begin with) never visits it either. Genuinely invisible, confirmed by
tracing the real code rather than assumed.

**Tried on `buildRows_` first, and not kept there.** The natural fix -- drive the day's
population from the day's own initial deck instead of the current one, the identical principle
Part 74 just gave the dashboard -- was built and tested against `api/_lib/expdf.js` first. It
turned out to change nothing reachable: `expdfCore`'s raw rows feed exactly three callers
(`expdfMine`, `expdfReport`, `expdfLeader`), every one of which filters by
`RECYCLE_ROLES.includes(r.role)` before anything else, and `expdfWeekCompute_`'s own internal
bookkeeping (`cells`, keyed `role|leader|ref`) filters the SAME way before a row ever reaches its
own output -- so a customer with no real current-row data to assign a role from (the initial
deck carries no status, no disbursement date, nothing `assignFor` needs) has nowhere to surface
on any of those three screens, with or without the fix. Confirmed empirically: a direct test
against `expdfWeekCore`'s own raw output, for exactly this customer, on a CLOSED week (where
Part 74's reasoning said the fix should reach further than the ghost mechanism ever could)
still came back absent -- not because the day was unmeasured, but because the row was being
built and then immediately discarded by the week's own role-keyed `cells` map. Reverted rather
than shipped: code with no observable effect anywhere is exactly the "half-finished
implementation" this repository's own rules already warn against, however reasoned the path to
it was.

**Kept on `expectedDefaulters` instead** -- the one screen in this system built to list every
customer rather than one leader's own book (the actual "Orodha / List of expected defaulters"
this whole thread started from), and the one screen that does NOT organize its rows by role at
all. A customer on today's own initial deck with no current-type row, ever, now gets a row
there too: status CLEARED, `arrears` 0, `recovered` the full initial amount (the same
absence-is-the-signal rule the ghost mechanism already follows), `role`/`phase` left `null`
rather than guessed (never a fabricated rotation slot), `leader` reading the same
`'(unassigned)'` sentinel this screen already uses for "nobody to credit." Bucketed into the
existing `dist[0]` ("cannot be placed on a weekday") the same way an unreadable disbursement
date already is; counted into every grand total the same way any other row is.

**What it costs.** Nothing: `iniSnap.rows` (today's own initial deck) was already read at the
top of this function for the existing baseline lookup; this only adds a second pass over data
already in memory. No new read, `test/speed.test.mjs` unaffected. No front-end file touched, so
`BUILD`/`CALL_BUILD` stay as Part 74 left them.

**Checked.** A new test proves the row appears, with the exact figures above, and that
`dist`/`initial` correctly include it. `npm test`: 1,531 pass (one net new test -- the two
tests written for the `buildRows_` attempt were removed along with the code they were testing,
since neither exercised anything that would not have passed identically before it).

**Not done, and said so rather than silently expanded:** the dedicated Exp.Def Report, the
phone's own worklist, and the leader-tap view all remain exactly as they were -- a customer
with no real current-row data genuinely has no leader to be credited to, and inventing one
would be a worse defect than the invisibility it replaced.

## Part 76 — A production incident: Expected Defaulters hung past 45 seconds, "Imeshindikana / Could not load"

> "expected defaulters - Imeshindikana / Could not load. Seva haijibu ndani ya sekunde 45 / the
> server did not answer within 45 seconds" -- the owner, 14 Nov 2026, minutes after confirming
> `db/RUN-ME-055` (Part 71's ghost-rows migration) had just been run for the first time.

That was the real trigger, confirmed rather than guessed: the owner pasted back the three
read-only confirmations (`idx_def_snap_team_ref`, `defaulter_ghost_rows`, and Part 74's
`expdf_recovery_totals`) moments before reporting the hang. Until that run, every call to
`defaulter_ghost_rows()` on the live book had always failed fast with Postgres's own "function
does not exist" (`readGhosts_`'s documented, graceful fallback) -- never a real query. The
owner's run was the FIRST time this function ever actually executed against the live book
rather than the 2.27-million-row synthetic fixture Part 71 measured it against, and the real
query ran long enough to burst straight through the portal's own 45-second client-side fetch
timeout (the same ceiling `DASH_PREV_BUDGET_MS`'s own comment in `portal-core.js` already names:
"well inside the client's 45 seconds").

**The root cause, traced rather than assumed:** `ghostRowsFor_`'s `budgetMs` parameter is
honoured through `withinMs_` -- a real `Promise.race` against a `setTimeout`, abandoning a slow
read without cancelling it (it keeps running underneath and warms the cache for the next
caller). `expdfMine` (the phone's own sacred-path worklist) has always passed `GHOST_BUDGET_MS`
(800ms) into this. **Four other callers passed `0` -- no ceiling at all** -- on the explicit,
documented theory that "this is not the sacred call path, it can wait out the rare slow read":
`expectedDefaulters` (`portal-core.js`, the exact screen reported), `expdfReport` and
`expdfLeader` (both via `expdfCore`'s own default parameter), and `expdfWeekCompute_`'s own
direct call for the week view. That theory was never actually exercised against a lookup that
genuinely runs long, because until today every one of those four calls hit the fast,
error-fast path instead. "Can wait longer than the phone" was always the real intent -- the
dashboard's own `DASH_PREV_BUDGET_MS`/`DASH_FLOORS_BUDGET_MS` (6000/8000ms) already do exactly
that, safely, for the same reason -- but "wait out the rare slow read" had been read, in these
four places, as "wait forever," and the live book's first real run proved that reading wrong.

**The fix.** One new constant, `GHOST_REPORT_BUDGET_MS` (5000ms, `api/_lib/expdf.js`) -- sized a
little tighter than the dashboard's own report-side budgets since these four screens stack this
read alongside several others in the same request -- with an env-var override
(`ghostReportBudgetMs_()`) mirroring `DASH_MONTH_BUDGET_MS`'s own existing idiom exactly, so a
test can shrink it instead of genuinely waiting several seconds out. All four call sites now
pass it: `expdfCore`'s own default parameter (fixing `expdfReport` and `expdfLeader`'s day/month
case for both at once, from the one shared default), `expdfWeekCompute_`'s direct call (fixing
the week view for both), and `expectedDefaulters`'s own direct call. `expdfMine` is untouched --
it already had its own, tighter, phone-safe budget.

**One rule, not four separately-reasoned exceptions to it.** This was never only
`expectedDefaulters`'s bug -- the identical "no budget here" comment, word for word, was copied
into `expdfWeekCompute_` ("the way `expectedDefaulters` already does"), and `expdfCore`'s own
default parameter silently carried the same `0` into both `expdfReport` and `expdfLeader`. The
house's own standing lesson from #671/#673 ("look for the OTHER places that pick") applied here
without having to be asked: all four were fixed in this one change, not just the one the owner
happened to hit first.

**A real test-writing hazard, found while building the regression test, worth keeping in mind
for the next one.** The first draft of the new test simulated the hang with a literal
`new Promise(() => {})` -- a promise that truly never settles, ever -- passed through the real
`fakeDb`/`FakeRpc` stack rather than a hand-rolled stub. `Promise.race` abandons it correctly, as
designed, but the abandoned promise itself is left permanently dangling, and node's own test
runner notices: that test failed with `cancelledByParent`/"Promise resolution is still pending
but the event loop has already resolved," and -- more seriously -- **took every later test in the
same file down with it** (confirmed directly: running the file standalone showed dozens of
unrelated, otherwise-passing tests cascade-fail the same way once that one test ran). The
codebase already had the safe answer to this, in `DASH_MONTH_BUDGET_MS`'s own existing test: a
mock that resolves LATE (a real `setTimeout`, here 250ms, well past the test's own shrunk 20ms
budget) rather than one that never resolves at all. Rewritten that way, the same assertions pass
cleanly, in well under a second, and a deliberate regression (reverting one call site back to
`0`) was confirmed to make the rewritten test fail for the right reason before this shipped.

**What it costs.** Nothing new: no new read, no change to round-trip count on any screen
(`test/speed.test.mjs` unaffected -- a budget bounds how long an existing call is waited for,
not how many calls are made). No read on `/api/upload` or `/api/call` either way.

**Checked.** One new test (`test/portal.test.mjs`) drives `expectedDefaulters`, `expdfLeader`
(day) and `expdfReport` (week) through the real `portalApi` dispatch with a slow ghost RPC and a
shrunk budget, proving each returns well inside it; confirmed to fail on a deliberate revert of
one call site before being kept. `npm test`: 1,532 pass. No front-end file touched, so
`BUILD`/`CALL_BUILD` stay as Part 75 left them -- this is a server-only fix.

**Not done:** whether the live book's own `defaulter_ghost_rows()` timing should be measured
directly (the synthetic fixture's own worst case was 86-115ms; the live book clearly runs
longer, by how much is not known from here, since a chat has no database access) is left open --
the budget makes the symptom impossible regardless of the real number, but the real number
itself would still be worth knowing, from the owner's own side, the next time the SQL editor is
open.

## Part 77 — The never-once-current rows (Part 75) land on their own real days, not "No date," not "today"

> "i think you added no-date instead of customers staying in their respective initial defaulters
> days... each day is independent" and, a few minutes later, after a first correction still
> missed the point: "i already said that we already know their days due disb date column but
> you just distract me man" -- the owner, 14 Nov 2026, the same hour Part 76 shipped.

Part 75's own never-once-current rows (a customer on today's own initial deck with no
current-type row, ever) carried `primary: 0, secondary: 0` -- the same "No date" bucket an
unreadable disbursement date already uses. The owner's first message said that bucket was
wrong; the first fix (`primary` set to TODAY's own weekday) answered a question nobody asked --
the owner's second message named the actual answer directly: `disb_date` is a column on
`defaulter_snapshots` itself, present on an INITIAL row exactly as it is on a CURRENT one, so
this ref's own real disbursement date was sitting on the row the whole time. `iniSnap`'s own
column list (`portal-core.js`) only ever asked for `ref, team, arrears` -- now widened to
include `disb_date` -- and the never-once-current row's own `primary`/`secondary` are computed
by the identical formula every current-deck row already uses (`isoWeekday(disb_date)`, then +3
days wrapped), landing it on its own real two cycle days, the same as anyone else. A ref whose
initial row somehow carries no `disb_date` at all still falls back to "No date" honestly --
checked directly, in a second, separate test -- since that case genuinely has nothing to read.

**A test that was testing the bug, not guarding against it.** The dedicated test for this case
(Part 75) built its fixture through the suite's own `D()` helper, which sets a real `disb_date`
(2026-07-21, a Tuesday) on every row by default -- so this exact scenario had a real date
available the whole time, and the test's own assertion (`dist[0] === 1`, "bucketed as undated")
was asserting the first cut's bug as if it were the feature, because the code never read the
column the fixture had already given it. Rewritten to assert the real days (`primary`/
`secondary`/`disb_date` on the row; `dist[2]`/`dist[5]` up by one against an identical
before/after fixture, since the baseline book already has other customers on those same two
days -- an absolute count would have been the wrong proof).

**What it costs.** One column added to a read the screen already makes (`disb_date`, alongside
`ref`/`team`/`arrears`); no new read, no change to round-trip count, `test/speed.test.mjs`
unaffected. No read on `/api/upload` or `/api/call`.

**Checked.** The existing test rewritten to prove the row lands on its own real Tue/Fri, not
"No date"; one new test proving the honest fallback still holds when a ref's own initial row
genuinely carries no date either. `npm test`: 1,533 pass. Server-only -- `BUILD`/`CALL_BUILD`
stay as Part 76 left them.

## Part 78 — The Exp.Def week keeps a day's own initial-only customer too, unassigned, never guessed

**"as i said we have initial of a day, i expect that customer in initial never to get lost even
if cleared its amounts and statuses that change"** -- the owner, 14 Nov 2026, read against the
real Thursday 12 Nov / ref 4231948032 case (Part 77's own re-examination): that ref's own
initial deck for that day carried it, 15,500, Chronic; that same day's own current deck did
not. Part 69/70's "keep a customer on their own initial deck" rule (`buildRows_`) only ever
WIDENS the filter for a row already present in `curRows` -- it has never been able to
SYNTHESIZE a row for a ref that is in `baseBy` but entirely absent from `curRows`, the harder
case both Parts named and left. Part 75 closed that harder case for `expectedDefaulters`
alone, for TODAY alone. This closes it for `expdfWeekCompute_`'s own per-day loop, for every
day of the week, not only today.

**Why this is not the all-time ghost, and must never be confused with it.** `expdfWeekCompute_`
already carries one rescue of this shape -- the all-time ghost (Part 71, `ghostRowsFor_`/
`db/RUN-ME-055`) -- but that one answers "missing from the team's LATEST data right now," and
is deliberately reached only through the week's own TODAY iteration: "the one thing this
feature's own design refuses to do anywhere else" is judge a past day by a fact only true
today. Read against that rule, Thursday 12th stays correctly excluded (Part 77) -- the gap is
real, but it was never the all-time ghost's to close. The new mechanism here, a **day-ghost**,
reads only ONE day's own two files: a ref on day `d`'s own initial deck, absent from day `d`'s
own current deck -- nothing about today, nothing borrowed from any other day -- so it can never
contradict Part 71's own scope, and it costs no new read at all (`ini.rows` and `cur.rows` for
day `d` are already fetched by the existing loop).

**What it cannot do honestly: name who should be credited.** `buildRows_`'s `assignFor` needs
fields (`days_elapsed`, `chronic_date`, `expire_date`) that live only on a CURRENT-type row, and
a day-ghost has none for day `d` by definition. Reaching back to find the ref's own current-type
row as of some earlier day is real, separate work -- a new, date-bounded database lookup;
`RUN-ME-055`'s own function takes no date parameter and only ever answers "right now" -- and it
is not guessed at here. A day-ghost is instead kept VISIBLE and its recovery COUNTED, with role,
phase and cycle left `null` and leader reading the honest `'(unassigned)'` sentinel this system
already uses for exactly this "nothing to credit" case (Part 75). It is kept OUT of
`expdfWeekCompute_`'s own `cells` (every existing row there is keyed `role|leader|ref` and
later filtered by `periodRows_`'s `RECYCLE_ROLES.includes(r.role)` -- a `null` role would be
silently dropped by that filter in every caller, `expdfReport` and `expdfLeader` alike, which
is exactly why this is NOT fed through the normal pipeline) and returned on its own, as
`unassignedCleared`, which `expdfReport` folds into a new top-level field of the same name
(`{customers, initial, recovered, rows}`) -- never into `sections` or the grand `totals`, which
stay exactly what they were, so nothing already shipped and tested changes shape or figure.
`expdfLeader` needs no change at all: a day-ghost has no leader, so it was never going to appear
on anyone's own card regardless.

**Scoped tightly, on purpose.** Only `expdfWeekCompute_`'s own per-day loop is touched.
`buildRows_`, `expdfCore` and `expdfMine` -- the sacred `/api/call` path -- are untouched, and so
is `expectedDefaulters` (Part 75's own, separate fix, which already covers its own screen). The
identical gap sits in `expdfCore`'s single-day and month readings too (used by `expdfReport`'s
day/month views) -- **flagged, not fixed here**: closing it there means touching `buildRows_` or
`expdfCore` directly, both shared with the phone, a bigger and separate decision than this one.

**What it costs.** Nothing new is read: `INI_COLS_` widens by one column (`disb_date`, the same
column Part 77 already widened `portal-core.js`'s own initial read to carry, for the identical
reason -- a day-ghost's own cycle day comes from its own initial row, never guessed). The per-day
diff is a plain in-memory Set lookup against data the loop already holds. `test/speed.test.mjs`
is unaffected; no read on `/api/upload` or `/api/call`.

**The front end.** The Exp.Def Report's week view gains one more board, "Cleared, no leader on
record for the day," shown only when the week actually has one of these rows -- ref, team, the
cycle day read off its own initial row, initial and recovered. It sits after the three
GMO/MANAGER/BIKE boards and before their shared footnote, built from `board()` the same as every
other table on this screen, so it inherits the same sort, totals and styling for free. `BUILD
2026-11-15-a`.

**Checked.** A new test (`test/portal.test.mjs`) adds a customer to one day only (Wednesday) of
the existing seven-day week fixture, on that day's own initial deck alone, sharing that day's
real upload batch (a different batch string would have tripped the unrelated "latest batch per
team+weekday" rule and silently dropped the fixture's own real rows for that day -- caught
before the fix was confirmed, not a bug in the fix itself): proves it is counted in
`unassignedCleared` with the right initial/recovered and its own real cycle day; proves the
existing "sum of its days" test's own grand total and customer count are byte-for-byte
unchanged by its presence; proves no role section and no named leader's own card ever shows it;
and proves a day (not week) reading of the same screen carries no `unassignedCleared` field at
all, flagging the known, deliberately out-of-scope gap rather than leaving it unexplained.
`npm test`: 1,534 pass. No read on `/api/upload` or `/api/call`.

**Closed by Part 87.** The board, and the belief behind it (that the rotation needs a current-deck row), are gone: a
customer on a day's initial deck whom that day's current deck does not name is a row of their leader's book, on
the cycle days the rotation names, counted in every total, on the week and on the day alike. The board is empty by construction.

**The owner was right, and was first told otherwise.** On 14 Nov the answer given was that the
two cards read the same defaulter files by two formulas, on purpose. That described the code
correctly and missed the point: the code was wrong. An Expected Defaulter OF A DAY has had one
definition in this system since the tab of that name was built --

> "Every defaulter is visited twice a week and the two days are derived from the loan itself:
> the weekday it was disbursed on (Day 1) and three days later (Day 2)" -- `expectedDefaulters`,
> `api/_lib/portal-core.js`: the Mon..Sun pills of the Expected Defaulters tab. And the daily
> list of the Exp.Def Report: "on a daily reading, the customers whose cycle day it is"
> (`periodRows_`, `api/_lib/expdf.js`).

-- and the function behind the card (Part 73, `db/RUN-ME-056`) ported the Exp.Def Report's test
for "is this customer in the file" (`buildRows_`) and left out its test for "is today their
day" (`periodRows_`). Part 74 moved the driving table to the initial deck, which was right, and
carried the omission with it. So every tile summed the whole defaulter book: the population
"Weekly recovery trend" reads. The two could differ only by a customer whose arrears grew.
No rule was missing. The card did not follow the one there was.

**What a tile is now.** For day D and each team:

- **Who:** a customer on D's own INITIAL file ("i want the weekly cyle to be facts of the no
  of defaulters we really had, not who remained so the lists per day must come from initial
  files") whose Day 1 or Day 2 is D's weekday. Day 1 is the weekday of the disbursement date;
  Day 2 is three days later, wrapping the week, Monday 1 to Sunday 7 -- `buildRows_`'s own
  formula, `((primary - 1 + 3) % 7) + 1`, to the character. The date is read off the customer's
  row on the initial file; where that row has none, off the same customer's row on the same
  day's current file.
- **What came back:** initial arrears less the SAME day's current arrears, per customer, never
  negative; a customer the current file no longer names is recovered in full; a customer the
  initial file never named is not counted. Unchanged from Parts 73 and 74.
- **The percentage:** recovered over the initial arrears of that day's own list -- "opnly expeef
  is against total arrea of the day given".
- **A customer with no disbursement date** on either row has no day. The Exp.Def week already
  says what to do with one (Part 54): counted ONCE for the week, on the last day that carried
  them, never once per day. The same here, within the dates one call asks for; and not at all
  if the same customer was counted on a real cycle day among those dates. The tile says how
  many of its customers were counted that way.
- **A day counts when both its own files were filed on it** -- the Exp.Def week's own rule
  (`expdfWeekCompute_`). A customer missing from a current file that exists has cleared; a
  current file that does not exist yet says nothing about anybody. On the morning a day's
  initial file is in and its current file is not, the first function read every customer of
  the day as recovered in full; now that day answers nothing, its tile reads "not uploaded
  yet", and it fills in when the current file lands. Found while this change was waiting on
  its tests, by reading the function against the week's own loop one more time.
- **A team-day with both files and nobody on cycle** answers zeros and reads as uploaded. An
  absent row is what the card draws as "not uploaded yet", and a filed day must never read as
  that.

The tile now also says **how many customers** were on the day's list, so it can be laid beside
the Expected Defaulters tab's pill for the same weekday.

**`db/RUN-ME-057`, a new function under a new name** -- `expdf_cycle_recovery_totals`. The page
asks for that name. Until the file is run the function does not exist, the read answers
nothing, and the card says so: every tile reads "no answer yet" and a line under the card names
the file (`edrNote`). It does NOT go on showing the whole book's recovery under the Expected
Defaulters' name off the old function, which the file drops: one definition of a figure, and
silence reads as success. **The owner has to run it once**; its text was pasted in the chat.

**What was not touched.** "Weekly recovery trend" (the whole book, the standing of RUN-ME-032,
the commission board that pays on it), the Exp.Def Report, the Expected Defaulters tab, the
phone. Nothing on `/api/upload` or `/api/call` reads this.

**Seen in the same screenshot, read against its rule, and left.** The first card's TOTAL read
94,338,048 where its six filed tiles add to 75,856,074: the difference is Saturday's
18,481,974 exactly. Sunday had no file yet; the standing carries the latest files forward to a
day that has none ("the latest current defaulter file is to live until the next one is

commission board pays on, pinned by the test that ties the board's week to the dashboard's
(`test/portal.test.mjs`, "the board's week is the dashboard's week"). That is the rule as
written and it is not this change's to alter. Whether a day with no file of its own should add
to the week is the owner's to say.

**What it costs.** The same two files a day the old function read, the same way, with one more
column (`disb_date`) and a pass over the week's rows in memory. Measured on a real PostgreSQL,
old function and new in the same minute, on 2,267,118 rows (42 teams, 150 days, two files a
day, 180 customers a team a day, each customer with a disbursement date of their own): a full
week for every team, 294 rows in about 0.3 s (0.27 to 0.4 over five runs) against the old

the week's rows to temporary files and took up to 560 ms; the one shipped keeps them in memory
(`work_mem = 8MB`, for this function alone). The dashboard asks for it twice a load, this week and last, as before:
`test/speed.test.mjs` is unchanged.

**Checked.**
- **The function against its mirror, on a PostgreSQL.** The tests cannot run SQL, so they read

  A new check, `tools/db-checks/expdf-cycle-recovery-parity.mjs`, draws random weeks of decks

- **Two tests** (`test/portal.test.mjs`): a customer who is in Friday's file, pays 70,000 on

**Not read by anybody else, and what trying cost.** Three independent reviewers were started on
