an arrow press asks the server, repaints and opens nothing; the week survives a table search and the arrows still work after it; the floor; the list with its arrows, its way home, the week in its Excel title and the card moving with it; a customer name that is markup drawn as text; Enter on an arrow steps and does not open the list; two quick presses and a held-back answer; a failed read; leaving and returning; no ledger), which **fails on the code as it was**. **31 of 31 deliberate breaks** (13 of the server, 18 of the page) each turn a test or the browser check red (one, the card read off a wider set of notices than the list, changes nothing a figure can show on a database that already scopes, and is held by a source pin; ## Part 129 — Every paint wires the whole screen: the buttons and cards a table search or sort used to kill (23 Nov)

> "fix the handlers lost after table search" — the owner, 23 Nov 2026, on the finding of Part 128.

**What was wrong, and since when.** `paint()` / `paintNow_()` rebuild `#view` whole — `HEAD` (the cards, bars, buttons and notes a screen draws above its table) and the table together — and then wire what they drew: `wireTable`, `wireTableSearch`, `wireBar` (the bars, filters, week arrows and every module hook such as the Teams & Staff leaders card, the devices, advance and leave desks), `wireOfficerFind`. `wireForms()` — the one place that wires a screen's own buttons and cards by id (+ New demand notice, Recovered today and the letterhead links on the Legal tab; + New complaint, + New team, + New staff, + New role, + New code, + New setting, the Settings rows, the imprest form and rate table, the roles reset, the system switch...) — ran from `drawView_()` only, the full draw. A keystroke in the search box above a table (`wireTableSearch` → `paint(true)`), a sort (`paint()`), a filter or a pick (the modules' `paint(true)`) repaint the screen and never reached it, so every element it had wired was a fresh one with no handler until the tab was reopened. Verified in a real browser on the code as it stood (Part 128): on the Legal tab one keystroke in the search box and *Recovered today* and *+ New demand notice* stopped answering; on Teams & Staff *+ New team*. As old as the search box.

**What was built.** `wireForms()` runs with every paint, from `paintNow_()` (after `wireOfficerFind`) and from `paintHeadOnly()` (a screen with no table), and `drawView_()` no longer calls it a second time (it keeps its two once-only hooks, `bpWire_` and `imprestOpenDeepLink_`). The whole of `wireForms()` was read first to see that running it on every keystroke is safe: it only ASSIGNS on-handlers (`el.onclick = ...`, `oninput`, `onchange`: a second run replaces the first and never doubles it; there is no `addEventListener` in it), masks code boxes (`hopeSecrets`, which says it is safe to repeat and leaves a masked box alone), recomputes two previews from the boxes' current values (`adjHint`, the imprest `recalc`), sets a card's role and title, and starts no timer, no read and no focus (the one `.focus()` in it is inside a click handler). The HOPE Loan head buttons (`wireLn*`) are the same kind of assignment and run only in that workspace. **Cost, measured in Chromium on a register of 5,000 notices:** `wireForms()` 2.5 ms, inside a `paint(true)` of about 1.2 s that the keystroke was already paying for (`tools/browser-checks/portal-legal-week.mjs`, point 10).

**Found while measuring, not part of the ask and not changed:** a search keystroke on a big table rebuilds the whole table's HTML (about 1.2 s for 5,000 rows on this machine; the live Legal register is about 1,100 rows, the Follow-up list about 10,000). The search has no debounce. Offered in CHAT.md section 8.

**Checked.** `test/pages.test.mjs` (*every paint wires the whole screen...*): `paintNow_` and `paintHeadOnly` call `wireForms()` after `wireBar()`, `drawView_` does not call it again, and `wireForms` stays safe to repeat (no `addEventListener`, no timer, no focus by the wiring itself). `tools/browser-checks/portal-legal-week.mjs` point 3: after a search keystroke *Recovered today* opens its list and *+ New demand notice* opens the form, and after a sort too; `tools/browser-checks/portal-leaders-real.mjs`: after a search on Teams & Staff *+ New team* opens the form (**both points fail on the page as it was**, both pass now). Three deliberate breaks (`wireForms` taken out of `paintNow_`; out of `paintHeadOnly`; put back into `drawView_` as well) each turn a test or a browser check red. `BUILD 2026-11-23-b`.

**Cost, CLAUDE.md section 1.** Nothing on the server: no read anywhere; `/api/upload` and `/api/call` untouched. On the page: 2.5 ms per repaint on a 5,000-row screen.

**Not done, said plainly.** Nothing seen on the live screen. The search's own cost on a big table (above) is not changed. Elements a module wires inside its own view function after a `setTimeout` (none were found; the modules wire through `wireBar`'s hooks) would still need the same treatment if one is ever written that way.

## Part 131 — The second reader of #775 read the week arrows: seven things it reproduced, all put right (23 Nov)

The rule of CHAT.md section 7: merge first, then one reader, nothing owed. One reader (its own scripts, the real page against the real `portalApi` over the repository's fake database) read #775 after it was live; **every finding was reproduced by hand on the merged code with the reader's own probes before it was believed**, and all seven were real. Its main-flow reading agreed with Part 128 (right figures, right weeks, scope held, two trips for another week, no leak between users or tabs).

**What was true and is fixed** (`public/app.html`, `public/mod/legal.js`, `api/_lib/portal-core.js`; `BUILD 2026-11-23-d`):

1. **Enter or Space on the card's "Back to this week" link opened the list instead of going back.** The link's keydown bubbled to the card (`role=button`, `onkeydown="lgWeekKey_"`), which cancelled the link and opened the list. It is a **button** now (`.lgwkhome`): Enter and Space are a native click, its keydown never reaches the card.
2. **A reader whose scope holds no notice had an endless backward arrow.** `legalSince_` answered null, the page read null as "no bound", and a code whose teams were never served a notice could step back week after week, two trips a press. The server now answers **this week as the floor** when there is no notice (`since: legalSince_(notices) || thisWeek`), so the arrow is off; an older server's answer with no `since` at all still reads as unbounded (the page's fallback, unchanged).
3. **A quiet refresh of a remembered Legal screen put the card back on this week after an arrow press.** Re-opening the tab inside the remembered-screen window paints the old screen and reads the register again behind it; the view's new HEAD then replaced the card. The chosen week now rides with the screen (`S.args.lgWeek`, snapshotted with the remembered screen and cleared by `go()` on a tab switch): the view keeps the arrows' answers on a quiet refresh and draws the card on the kept week (`lgWeekKept_`). Coming back to the tab inside the remembered-screen window therefore finds the week the reader left it on, exactly as a remembered screen keeps its filters; a fresh open (after the window, or after anything that forgets the remembered screens: any non-read call does) starts on this week.
4. **A slow answer for a list the reader had closed re-opened it and painted the card back to its week, over a later arrow press.** Every list asked for has a ticket (`LGW_.listSeq`); an answer is **stale** when a later list was asked for, the card was moved to another week, or the list was closed, and a stale answer, good or bad, paints nothing.
5. **In the dark theme the way-home link was nearly unreadable** (the browser's default link blue on the lit card: 1.67:1). The button takes its colour from the theme (`--b700` light, `--b300` dark; both over 4.5:1, measured in the kept check).
6. **A keyboard press on the list's arrows dropped the focus to the page body**, so the next Enter did nothing. The arrow pressed keeps the focus across the redraw (`focusArrow`), as the card's arrows already did.
7. **A failed step inside the list left a dead end**: the error replaced the whole drawer, week bar included. The last good list's week bar is kept above the error, so the reader can try again or go home.

**The reader's test gaps, taken:** the kept browser check now presses the way home with Enter and Space, reads a scope with no notice, holds a list's answer and a register read to make the two races, presses the list's arrow from the keyboard twice, and fails a step inside the list (`tools/browser-checks/portal-legal-week.mjs`, section 11: 66 points on the page as fixed; **run against the page as merged in #777 it reads 53 pass and 13 red of 66: every one of the seven is red**); `test/portal.test.mjs` pins the floor for a scope with no notice (the list and the tab's own card); `test/pages.test.mjs` pins the button, the ticket, the stale test, the kept focus, the kept bar and the kept week. **Deliberate breaks:** the seven fixes broken one at a time, one of them two ways (the way home a link again; no floor with no notice; a quiet refresh forgetting the week, and the card drawn on this week whatever was kept; a stale answer painting; the way home with no colour of its own; the arrow losing the focus; a failed step dropping the bar): **8 of 8 each turn a pin, the portal test or the browser check red.** **Not taken:** the check still runs at one width (1,400 px; the reader found the layout right at 360 px by its own probe) and stays outside `npm test` (it needs a browser).

**Cost, CLAUDE.md section 1.** Nothing on the server's reads (`since` is computed from rows already held); nothing on `/api/upload` or `/api/call`; `test/speed.test.mjs` unchanged.

**Mistakes of mine (Part 128's, and one of this Part's).** Four of the seven were races and keyboard paths the kept check never tried; the "no bounds" unit test pinned the very behaviour behind finding 2 without separating an older server from "no notice in scope"; and the check's "a press on the disabled arrow asks nothing" counted server calls only (it would also pass with no arrow at all): it now reads the arrow's own disabled state first (section 11). **And the first form of the new "slow answer for a closed list" point was vacuous on BOTH pages:** it held the server's answer for the week key `''`, but a list opened from the card asks for the card's OWN week (its `data-mon`), so the hold never applied and the point passed on the page as merged for no reason that was the fix. Found by reading the merged-page log line by line before committing (the point was not among the red ones); the hold is now keyed on the card's week, and the point is red on the page as merged. The lesson is CHAT.md section 7's: a point of a check is believed only once it has been seen red on the code it was written against, and the log of that run is read line by line, not by its totals.

**Not done, said plainly.** Nothing seen on the live screen; the reader's probes live in the chat's scratch folder and are not kept (the kept check carries the same points).

## Part 132 — One Miamala, both expected books (23 Nov)

> "single input of Miamala should reflrct in both initial and current expected reports since miamala are always already collected so early collection officers are lalamenting why it doesnt count for them" — the owner, 23 Nov 2026.

**What it was.** The Iliyonasia register (Part 14 and after) keyed every entry under the book it was typed against, and the two expected books were two figures on purpose: an entry filed as *Expected — Current* moved the day's Col (the weekly report, the dashboard's Col trend and strip, the Orodha, the month ledger's `c` cells, the phone's Col) and never early collection; one filed as *Expected — Initial* moved early collection (the `ecol` cells, the Early Collection tile, the early scheme on the commission board) and never the day's Col. The data clerk files a Miamala once, against one book, so whichever book they chose, the other never saw the money: the early collection officers were the ones left out, and said so.

**The rule now.** A Miamala is money received and verified: it was collected on the day and it was collected early alike. **One entry against EITHER expected book counts in BOTH**, decided in ONE place, where the register is keyed (`adjReceived_`, `api/_lib/adjustments.js`): an expected entry goes into the per-team, per-day, per-cell and per-ref keys of both books, and into both books' totals and counts; the row itself keeps the book it was typed against (the register is the record of what was typed). Every screen that reads the register through `adjReceived_` follows at once, with no change of its own: the weekly report and the leader reports, the dashboard (the Col trend, the strip's Col % and Early Collection %, the Orodha's T. and M. columns), the month ledger (`adjLedgerCells_`: the `c` and `ic` cells both take every expected entry) and so the month report and the presentation, the two expected-sheet screens, the phone's Col figure (the call path reads `expected-current` only and now sees initial-filed entries too: arithmetic on rows already read, no read added), and the commission board. **The arrears pair is untouched:** the morning and evening decks are two positions of one day, not two readings of one payment, and an entry against one of them stays on that one.

**The commission side, one test for both schemes.** The early scheme counts every customer an expected entry names, whichever book it was filed against (`adjCountableRefs_`, called once now for both schemes where it was called twice: the two lists of named customers are one list). "Already paid for" is asked of BOTH sheets: a customer the deck shows PAID or OVERPAID on EITHER sheet that day has been paid for by the deck, and the register pays for them a second time on neither scheme. The Iliyonasia tab makes the same judgement on every row (`countState`): *counted* on both books, or *superseded* with the sheet that shows them paid named in the note; `countBooks` says what each sheet shows (`paid` / `not paid`); the tab's `superseded` lead counts the rows the deck has overtaken. The form's hint under the book picker says, for either expected book, that today's collected AND early collection move together; the tab's two expected tiles say each book's net "counts in both expected books" (the tiles still show what was TYPED against each book, not what counts: what counts is the two added together, and that is said on the tile).

**The one new risk, and its probe.** Before this, somebody who wanted both books to move may have typed the same payment twice, once against each book; such a pair now counts twice. **`db/RUN-ME-086-expected-adjustments-filed-twice-read-only.sql`** (pasted in the chat, 2,508 characters, flush-left, one read-only statement, END line) lists every such pair on the live book: same report date, same team (blanks and case aside; no team is no team), same customer ref (blank is blank), same amount, one entry of each expected book; newest first, the register's own words, and a last COUNT row of the entries listed. It changes nothing; which of each pair to delete is the owner's, on the tab. Not built, on purpose: a rule that drops a twin at read time would decide that two equal amounts are one payment, which a register cannot know.

**Cost (CLAUDE.md section 1).** Nothing on `/api/upload`. On `/api/call`: no read added; the sync's Col figure loops twice per expected row where it looped once (microseconds). The commission board makes one deck read for the named customers where it made two. `test/speed.test.mjs` unchanged (its budgets are ceilings).

**Checked.** `test/portal.test.mjs`: three tests (the early scheme pays for the customer a day-sheet entry names, and its percentage moves; the dashboard's Col trend and strip move by an initial-filed entry; the strip's Early Collection tile moves by a day-sheet entry; the register's keys for both books equal, the arrears pair apart; the tab's judgement by both sheets, row by row, and the commission board agreeing with it); the register's seventeen older tests unchanged and green; `test/pages.test.mjs` pins the hint's words and the two tiles; `test/expected-adjustments-twice.test.mjs` (3 pins: one read-only statement under 10,000 characters, the pair test on every key, the arrears books never read, the COUNT row, the collation-proof order; the kept check's breaks each naming text that is in the file once); the kept check `tools/db-checks/expected-adjustments-twice.mjs` on a PostgreSQL 16 with the register made from `db/schema.sql`'s own block (a pair, a triple, the same payment twice against ONE book, four near misses, a team in another case with a blank, the whole book, the arrears books, an expected entry whose twin is an arrears entry; every printed row against a model written again; the table byte-identical; a register with no pair; a book without the register refused; the text cut at every line: refused or answered whole, never a partial answer; **11 of 11 deliberate breaks caught**); deliberate breaks of the change: **9 of 10 each turn a test red** (the old one-book keying; an arrears entry keyed under the expected books; both books keyed but one counted; the commission asking the initial sheet alone; the tab judging by one sheet; the tab's day-sheet reading; the hint's words; the tiles' words; the file pairing an entry with its own book); the tenth, the collection board's own count list emptied, changes nothing anybody sees, because the PMO board (`api/_lib/pmo.js`) reads no customer count at all (an equivalent mutant: the list is kept for the day sheet's `paid_n`, a display count on other screens, as it was).

**Mistakes of mine, found by the check before the file was handed over.** The first form's COUNT row could not be matched to the PAIR rows by type (numeric against text); its pair condition was written twice, in both branches of the union, so seven of the deliberate breaks could not be applied once (a CTE now finds the pairs once); its "count of pairs" was undefined for a payment filed three times (it counts entries now); and its ORDER BY compared raw team and ref text, which the live book's en_US collation and a scratch one order differently (plain code-point order now, `collate "C"`).

**Not done, said plainly.** Nothing seen on the live screen; how many pairs the live book holds is not known until RUN-ME-086 is run; a pair counts twice until one of its rows is deleted; the two tiles on the Iliyonasia tab still show each book's own net as typed.

## Part 133 — The cure of Part 129 proved on every screen that loads: nine screens, a repaint nobody typed, the letterhead links that never reached their module, and what `wireForms()` may and may not do (23 Nov)

> The brief this chat was given for the matter Part 128 found: "find the safest cure and prove it on more than one screen ... do not slow any screen down, do not change what a screen shows ... break the fix on purpose ... say plainly what was not done."

**What happened, said first.** While this chat read all of `wireForms()` and built the proof, the chat that wrote CHAT.md merged the same cure as #776 (Part 129): `wireForms()` is run by `paintNow_()` and `paintHeadOnly()` and no longer by `drawView_()`. The two chats arrived at the same two lines independently, and this chat's own copy of them was dropped when its branch was restarted from `main`. **What follows is what #776 did not have:** the proof on every screen that loads, a trigger it did not name, one defect it left, and tests that RUN `wireForms()` instead of reading it.

**How far the defect reached (the page as it was before #776, commit `0e126a4`).** A real browser, the real page, the real `portalApi` over the fake database, every screen that loads (48 views, 41 with a table search): after ONE keystroke in the table search, nine screens had lost handlers from their head, and the other 32 had lost nothing. Legal: today's recovery card, the six letterhead links, **+ New demand notice**. Teams & Staff: **+ New team**, **+ New**, **+ Agent** and every staff and agent row. PMO deductions: **+ New case**, **Report**. Complaints, Restructuring and HR staff: their one **+ New** button each. Adjust: the target's hint, the amount box, Save. **The Imprest request form: the role box, every fare and night box (so the live total), and Send.** Imprest approval: the state chips, the rate editor, the phone-alert policy. #776 had seen Legal and Teams & Staff.

**A repaint nobody typed.** `tipsStart()` asks for the hints 2.5 seconds after sign-in and, when they arrive, repaints the list on screen so the colours appear (`if (document.getElementById('mainCard')) paint(true)`). **Verified on the page as it was before #776, nobody touching it:** the Legal tab drew and **+ New demand notice** answered; four seconds after the page opened the tab had been repainted once, by itself, and the button was dead. The portal opens on the tab a person last used (`lastView_()`), so on those nine screens the buttons went dead about three seconds after opening. Whether an earlier report of a button not working (the imprest request's Send is quoted in the comments of `wireForms()`) was this is not known.

**What `wireForms()` is: all 420 lines read before anything was said about repeating it.**

| What it does | Repeat-safe? |
|---|---|
| `window.hopeSecrets()`: masks `input[data-secret]` boxes not yet masked | yes: one scan; brand.js marks a masked box (`data-secret-on`) and leaves it alone |
| the HOPE Loan wirers `wireLnCs_`, `wireLnFinance_`, `wireLnReversals_`, `wireLnGm_`, `wireLnAssessPlan_` (only in that workspace) | yes: `.onclick` / `.onchange` assigned to elements looked up by id (`public/mod/loan.js`) |
| about 30 buttons and links by id, and nine families by attribute (`[data-agent]`, `[data-staff]`, `[data-role]`, `[data-skey]`, `[data-code]`, `[data-user]`, `[data-impq]`, `[data-rle]`, `[data-rld]`) and `input[name^="pp_"]` | yes: an assignment replaces |
| today's recovery card: `cursor`, `role`, `tabindex`, `title`, two handlers | yes: set on the element that is there |
| `adjHint()`; the Imprest request form's `recalc()` | yes: they read the page they are on (fare, nights, total, whether Send is open, the line saying why) |

**It starts nothing:** no timer, no request, no listener on the document or the window, no focus; every `srv()`, `render()`, `go()`, `drawer()`, `confirm()` and `toast()` in it is inside a handler. **Once per keystroke it does** 44 lookups of an id by name, eleven scans of the page for an attribute (ten in `wireForms()`, one in `hopeSecrets()`) and two writes that read the page.

**A second defect, found by the kept check and fixed here.** The letterhead links on the Legal tab (set logo, stamp, signature, signatory, title, phone; admin only) call `settingForm()`, which lives in the **admin** module. That module loads when Settings or Teams & Staff opens, not when Legal does, so **in a session that opened Legal first, a click threw `ReferenceError: settingForm is not defined`**, repaint or no repaint, and #776 as merged still did. The handler now asks for the module (`modLoad_('admin')`, which answers at once when it is in) and then calls `settingForm`; if the module cannot be fetched the loader's own words are said as an error. These links are the only place `wireForms()` calls into a module its element does not come from (read, every handler: the others are drawn by the module that owns their function).

**Why this cure and not the others** (the choice was #776's and this chat's alike). *Inline handlers screen by screen* (what the weekly card did): nine screens, about fifty elements and the rows of four tables, each with its own chance to miss one, and the next screen built the old way is dead again. *Not rebuilding the head on a table-only repaint*: it would keep typed values too (below), but several screens call `paint()` after changing `HEAD` and rely on it being redrawn (`frSet_` in the fraud module, `presRedraw_`), so it changes what every one of sixty screens does on a repaint.

**What was built here** (`public/app.html`, `BUILD 2026-11-23-d`): the letterhead handler above; a note at the top of `wireForms()` and a paragraph in #776's comment above `drawView_()` saying what it may do now that every paint runs it and that a keystroke is not the only repaint; the two comments of #775 that said a repaint drops what `wireForms()` attached are corrected (the weekly card stays inline for its own reason: every arrow press replaces the card in place, with no paint after it).

**Cost, CLAUDE.md section 1.** Nothing on `/api/upload` or `/api/call` (a change to the portal page); no read added to any screen (one keystroke makes no request: counted on all nine screens). **Measured** on the Legal tab's 22-column table: `wireForms()` 0.15 ms on 500 rows (a repaint 76 ms), 3.0 ms on 5,000 rows (a repaint 965 ms), 1.7 ms on 3,000 rows (a repaint 537 to 572 ms): about a third of one per cent of the repaint it joins (#776 measured 2.5 ms on 5,000 notices). The only new cost to anybody is the admin module (one script, fetched once) the first time somebody presses a letterhead link before opening Settings or Teams & Staff.

**Checked.**

- `tools/browser-checks/portal-repaint-wiring.mjs` (new, a real browser, 52 points; `APP_FILE` runs it on another copy of `app.html`): every screen that loads, one keystroke and then a sort: no handler lost from any head, and the nine screens each really compared (41 of 48 views have a table search; the other seven never repaint through `paint()`); the page's own repaint at about three seconds; after a repaint the buttons **do their work** on each of the nine screens (the drawer that opens, three nights at the role's rate making a live total of 150,000 and opening Send, Send asking the server, the rate editor filling its boxes, the hint under the adjustment's target following the amount's sign, the form left in the state a first draw gives it), on Settings (no table: the head alone is drawn, the other road to the same wiring), and on the letterhead links in a session that has not loaded the admin module; today's card dressed again; three keys typed in a row land in the box, which keeps its focus and its caret; **one keystroke runs `wireForms()` once and makes no request, sets no timer, adds no listener to the document or the window**, and every paint wires the bar and the forms exactly once; the cost against the repaint. **On the page as it was before #776: 32 of 52 points fail. On #776 as merged (`BUILD 2026-11-23-c`): the 3 of the letterhead links fail and 49 pass: its cure holds on all nine screens. On this change: 52 of 52.**
- `test/pages.test.mjs`, four new tests, beside #776's pin of the two draw functions (it reads the source): **the draw functions RUN on stand-ins and the order of wiring is recorded** (a repaint, a paint that keeps no scroll, a full draw with a table, a full draw without); **`wireForms()` RUN on a stand-in page built from what it looks up** (the ids, the attribute selectors, and the pairs the letterhead links are looked up by), three times (a rebuilt page, then the same page again): every button answers a click, the card is dressed, the third wiring leaves it as the first, and **anything that starts something at wiring time (a timer, a request, a redraw, a drawer, a confirm box, a focus) fails the test**, every name a handler uses being left undefined so a wiring-time call of one is a `ReferenceError`; the names it calls are pinned (a new one must be added to the list, which is the moment somebody asks whether it is safe once per keystroke), a listener on the document or window is refused and nothing else calls it; the letterhead handler loads the module first and says so when it cannot. **On #776 as merged the letterhead test is the only one of the four that fails** (the other three guard the property its cure relies on, which was true).
- **Sixteen deliberate breaks of the cure** (what #776's pin, the new unit tests and the browser check each turned red; the browser's figure is its failing points of 52):
  | # | the break | #776's pin | the new unit tests | browser, points failing |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | `paintNow_()` no longer wires the forms | red | draw, names | 42 |
  | 2 | `paintHeadOnly()` no longer wires the forms | red | draw, names | 2 |
  | 3 | `drawView_()` wires again: a full draw wires twice | red | draw, names | 11 |
  | 4 | `wireForms()` run before `wireBar()` in `paintNow_()` | red | draw | none (the browser cannot see an order) |
  | 5 | a timer started at wiring time | red | stand-in | 9 |
  | 6 | a request made at wiring time | passes | stand-in | 9 |
  | 7 | a document listener added in `wireForms()` | red | stand-in, names, letterhead | 9 |
  | 8 | the letterhead links calling `settingForm` bare again | passes | letterhead | 3 |
  | 9 | `+ New demand notice` not wired | passes | stand-in | 2 |
  | 10 | access-code masking dropped from `wireForms()` | passes | stand-in, names | none (no masked box on a table screen to see) |
  | 11 | `paintNow_()` wires the forms twice | passes | draw, names | 19 |
  | 12 | `wireForms()` that works only once per page | passes | stand-in | 24 |
  | 13 | today's recovery card no longer dressed | passes | stand-in | 1 |
  | 14 | `BUILD` not bumped | passes | letterhead | none |
  | 15 | the Imprest form's `recalc()` dropped | passes | names (and an older pin) | 1 |
  | 16 | a head-only draw that no longer wires the bar | red | draw | 1 |

  Every break turns at least one unit test red; **nine of the sixteen pass #776's pin** (it reads the source: it cannot see what the function does), and the browser check catches thirteen. The first run of the browser check passed two more (the form's `recalc()` dropped; a head-only draw without the bar) for want of a point: the form's state after a repaint and a count of `wireBar()` were added, and now catch them.

**What a person will see.** The buttons and boxes in the head of those nine screens answer after typing in a table search, sorting, choosing a filter, and about three seconds after the portal opens (the first two were #776's; the third is the same cure, proved). The letterhead links open their setting in any session. Nothing else on any screen changes.

**Not done, said plainly.**

- **A repaint still clears what was typed into the head.** Verified before and after: on the Imprest request form, "DODOMA" in the destination and 3 nights become empty and 0 after one keystroke in the table search below it; the Adjust amount likewise; the hints repaint at about three seconds does the same to a form started within the first three seconds. The form is alive again after a repaint but empty. The cure is not rebuilding the head on a table-only repaint (above): offered, not done (CHAT.md section 8).
- **`wireOfficerFind()` adds one listener to the document for every repaint of the Calls report** (counted: one per keystroke in its table search, on the page as it was and as it is; each holds on to the detached boxes of its own paint). Harmless in size and not caused by any of this; not touched.
- **HOPE Loan (`ln_*`) was not run in the browser:** the harness has no loan endpoint. Its five wirers were read and are assignments only; **the call app and the other pages were not touched.**
- **Not compared, 7 of the 48 views:** those with no table search (`expdfrep`, `findcust`, `bonusplan`, `checklist`, `teamtrend`, `settings`, `officerloc`); they never repaint through `paint()`, and Settings is covered by the head-only points. `bpWire_` (the bonus plan's boxes) guards itself with a `data-wired` mark and has no repaint.
- Nothing was seen on the live screen (a chat has no sign-in). No `hints` tip: there is nothing for a person to discover.

**Mistakes of mine.**

- **I built for hours a cure that had been merged while I worked.** I read `git log` at the start (it ended at #775, as CHAT.md said) and did not fetch `main` again until I went to push. Another chat had been given the same matter in the owner's words ("fix the handlers lost after table search") and merged it as #776. A chat that has been working for a while fetches `main` and reads the new Parts before it commits to a Part number.
- My first comment on `paintHeadOnly` claimed the same cause had left an access-code box clear after a repaint; I had not seen that on any screen (the only masked boxes are in Settings, which has no table). It was taken out before it was committed. A claim in a comment is checked like one in a message.
- The first form of the check's imprest point used the wrong column for the rate table (`rate` for `accommodation_per_day`), so the total read 0 on a screen that was working; its first form of the page's own repaint waited for a repaint after zeroing its counters, which on a slow machine could have raced the hints (it now counts from before sign-in); and its first run passed two breaks (the form's `recalc()` dropped; a head-only draw without the bar) for want of a point, which were then added.
- My first stand-in page for `wireForms()` was built only from ids written as literals and so missed the letterhead links and today's card, which are looked up through a list of pairs; the test said so by failing.

## Part 134 — The dashboard's Legal card opens its list and steps by week, like the Legal tab's (23 Nov)

> "the legal recovery card at dashboard should be able to openup too - with the backward and foward arrows as usual" — the owner, 23 Nov 2026.

**What it was.** The dashboard's *Legal recovery* KPI (Part 26) was a plain tile: today's recovery first, the week, the noticed customers and the owed beneath it, no tap and no arrows. The week behind it was the dashboard's own (the week bar at the top), and Part 128 had pointed the owner there when the Legal tab's card got its arrows. The owner wants the card itself to open and to step, as the Legal tab's does.

**What was built.** ONE card builder draws both cards. The server's `dashboardFull` answers `legal` as the same object the Legal tab's card and the list behind it read (`legalCard_`: the totals plus `today`, `mon`, `sun`, `thisWeek` and `since`), so the dashboard draws it with `lgWeekCard_` inside the `<!--lgw-->` markers, and everything of Parts 128 and 131 holds on the dashboard with no code of its own: a tap (or Enter / Space) opens the list of the week the card is on (`legalRecoveriesDrawer_`, with its own arrows, the lawyer column and the downloads), ◀ ▶ step the card by itself (one `legalRecoveries` read a week, kept two minutes, a late answer never painting over a later press), the way home, the focus kept, the stale-answer ticket, and the chosen week riding with the remembered screen (`S.args.lgWeek`) so a quiet refresh and a table search keep it. **Two things are the dashboard's own:** (1) the card keeps its name, and on this week it reads as it always did there, today's figure first with the week, the noticed customers and the owed beneath (`var dash = S.view === 'dashboard'` inside the builder; the Legal tab's card is unchanged); on another week, its own arrows' or the week bar's, the week's figure is the headline, since "today" is no day of that week; (2) **the week bar still moves the whole dashboard, and resets the card to the bar's week** (`wireWeekBar`: the typed date, the two steps and the way home each `delete S.args.lgWeek`), so the card and the boards never show different weeks for no reason; the card's ceiling is the REAL this week whatever week the bar is on (`realMon` in `dashboardFullCompute_`), so from a bar-past-week the card can step forward on its own. What the arrows remember is reset by one helper now (`lgWeekReset_`, called by the Legal tab's module and by the dashboard view; the chosen week of a quiet refresh is kept). **And a claim of Part 131 is made true by design:** coming back to a tab inside the remembered-screen window found the chosen week only if a quiet refresh had happened to land after the press and re-snapshot the screen (the kept check showed it on the dashboard, whose last load is never in flight at the press); `lgWeekPaint_` now puts the reading in `S.args` (`lgLegal`, `lgAt`) and tells the remembered snapshot (its HEAD and args) at once, and `lgWeekKept_` reads the args, not the shared two-minute cache, which the two screens share and each starts afresh on a fresh open.

**Cost (CLAUDE.md section 1).** Nothing on `/api/upload` or `/api/call`. The dashboard's own load reads nothing more (`legalCard_` is arithmetic on rows `dashboardFull` already held; `since` is a pass over the notices in scope). An arrow press on the dashboard is the Legal tab's two trips for another week (`test/speed.test.mjs`, unchanged); a tap is the list's read as before.

**Checked.** `test/portal.test.mjs`: the dashboard's `legal` carries the list's own `mon`, `sun`, `thisWeek`, `since` and `on` for last week, the week before and this week, its ceiling the real this week even when the dashboard is slid back, and the same `today` on this week. `test/pages.test.mjs`: the dashboard view draws the card by the one builder inside the markers and calls the reset helper; the builder, RUN with `S.view` dashboard, reads today's figure first on this week and the week's on another, with its own name, range, noticed customers and way home, and the Legal tab's card as it was; the three week-bar handlers reset the card; the module calls the helper. `tools/browser-checks/portal-legal-week.mjs` section 12 (the REAL page over the REAL `portalApi`, `dashboardFull` answered for real): the card on the dashboard with arrows on this week, today's figure first; ◀ steps the card alone while the week bar stays; a tap and Enter open the week's list; the bar slides the dashboard and the card follows it; from the bar's past week the card steps forward to this week on its own; the bar's way home; a quiet refresh of the remembered dashboard and a table search keep the card's week: 14 points (80 in all on the page as fixed); run against the page as merged in #779 it reads 66 pass and 4 red, the section's first three points red and its run stopped at the first arrow press, there being no arrow on that card. Deliberate breaks: **12 of 12 each turn a pin or the portal test red** (the old one-figure card drawn again; the card drawn on this week whatever was kept; the server's card with no bounds; the ceiling the bar's week; the week bar leaving the card's own week; the week figure as this week's headline; no reset on the dashboard; the reset helper forgetting a chosen week; the Legal module not resetting; the flavour decided by nothing; the remembered snapshot not told; the kept week reading the shared cache).

**Not done, said plainly.** Nothing seen on the live screen; the Presentation's Legal slide and the dashboard's two Legal boards still follow the week bar only (the boards are per lawyer; the card's own stepping does not move them, on purpose: the bar is where the boards' week is chosen); the check still runs at one width.

## Part 135 — When Finance closes the month, approvals close the same second on every server, and a refusal is never reported as a decision (23 Nov)

> "From next time, when finance manager closes advance request window – even approvals should be disabled so that people cant approve when he's already proceeding with already approved requests in time" — the owner, 23 Nov 2026.

**What was already true.** The finance manager's *Finalize* button on the Advance report (#588; the one setting `ADV_FINALIZED`, `advFinalize`) closes THIS month for new requests **and for decisions**: `advClosed_` makes `advDecide` skip a request of a finalized month ("closed -- this month is finalized"), `advRequest` refuses a new one, the desk lists the month's undecided requests under *closed by Finance* instead of *pending*, and the report marks every row `finalized`. The temporary reopen (`advReopen`, 24 hours unless `ADV_REOPEN_HOURS` says otherwise) opens it again for both. There was no window other than the month: nothing else in the code opens or closes advance requests. The owner was told so.

**What was not true: two faults, found by reading the code against the owner's words.**

1. *The closed state was read through the settings memo.* `settingGet` answers from a 20-second memo (`SETTINGS_TTL_MS`) kept per server instance, and a write drops the memo of the instance that made it and of no other. So when the finance manager pressed Finalize, every OTHER instance went on answering "open" for up to 20 seconds: a decision (and a new request) reached there was saved after the month had been closed, and `advFinalize` / `advReopen`, which write the whole JSON of months back, could write one instance's older answer over a newer one. No test covered a decision on a still-pending request after Finalize at all (the existing test finalizes, then tests requests).
2. *The desk told the approver "Approved" for a refusal.* A refused save (the month finalized, a request already decided, one that is not this desk's) comes back as `updated: 0` with the reason in `skipped`, and the advance desk's drawer, and the leave desk's, toasted `Imeidhinishwa / Approved` or `Imekataliwa / Disapproved` whatever the answer was (the bulk save said "Saved: 0 approved, 0 disapproved" in the same breath as the reason). An approver pressing Approve on a closed month read "Approved".

**What was built.** `settingFresh_(db, key)` (`api/_lib/portal-core.js`): one setting read straight from the database (one row by its key), the memo told what was read, a failed read falling back to the memo (a failed read is no reason to refuse a decision: the save that follows asks the same database). `advDecide` and `advRequest` read `ADV_FINALIZED` with it, in the same wave as the reads they already made, and so do `advFinalize` and `advReopen` (they write the whole JSON back). The display readers (`advQueue`, `advRequestPage`, `advReport`) still use the memo: they are re-read at the next load and the decision path is the guard. On the screens: the single-request drawer on both desks says `Haikuhifadhiwa / NOT saved:` and the server's reason, as an error, when nothing was saved, and closes and re-reads the screen so the closed month shows; the bulk save says the same instead of "Saved: 0". A saved decision says what it did, as before, with any side note. **No new rule:** Finalize is still the only close; the system does not close approvals by itself at a day or an hour.

**Cost (CLAUDE.md section 1).** Nothing on `/api/upload` or `/api/call`. An advance decision, a new request, a Finalize and a Reopen each make one more read of one row by its key, in the wave of reads they already ran (a staff action, a few hundred a month). `BUILD 2026-11-23-h` (two modules).

**Checked.** `test/portal.test.mjs`: a server instance whose memo says open, while another has finalized (the row is written without dropping this memo): a single decision either way, a bulk tick of two and a new request are all refused with their reasons and nothing is saved or recorded; the memo of this instance catches up; a reopen written by another instance is seen at once and a second Finalize closes it again at once; a reopen made from an instance that had not heard keeps another month's finalize. It fails on the code as it was at the first decision (`expected 0, actual 1`). `test/pages.test.mjs`: the real drawers and bulk saves of both desks are RUN against refused, saved, side-noted and empty answers; the four server functions are pinned to the fresh read and the fresh read to its one row, its memo update and its fall-back. **13 of 13 deliberate breaks each turn a test red** (each of the four functions back on the memo, the memo not told, the fall-back removed, the wrong key, each toast back to "Approved" or "Saved: 0", the error flag, the drawer left open).

**Not done, said plainly.** Nothing seen on the live book: the report that approvals continued after the finance manager closed the month is explained by the 20-second memo and by the toast, not reproduced; if approvals got through for longer than a few seconds after Finalize, the day and the name of who approved would settle it. A desk page already open when Finalize is pressed still shows its buttons until its next press or refresh; a press now says NOT saved and why. The system does not close approvals by itself at a set day or hour (no such rule exists; offered, not built). The leave desk has no Finalize (its Part 58 and 59 say why), so only its toast was corrected.
